claims.finding:
CONFIRMED, with one precision correction to the wording.

What the code actually does: Profiles DOES write an ownership marker. `tryLoad` stamps `data._lock = { jobId = game.JobId, ts = now }` inside its UpdateAsync transform (Profiles.luau:118). So it is not true that there is *no* marker — there is one. But it is a per-SERVER identity (`game.JobId`), not a per-LOAD token: no GUID/session id is generated per acquisition, so two successive loads of the same player on the same server produce an identical token, and there is nothing that distinguishes "this load" from "a previous load by the same job".

The operative half of the claim is exactly right and is the real defect: `_lock` is read in exactly ONE place in the whole module — `lockHeldByOther` (Profiles.luau:100), which is called only from `tryLoad`. The save path never looks at it. `trySave` (Profiles.luau:129-147) opens an UpdateAsync, blindly copies every OWNED_FIELDS key from the in-memory copy over `stored` (:134-136), and then either nils the lock (`stored._lock = nil`, :138, when release=true) or re-stamps itself as owner (`stored._lock = { jobId = game.JobId, ts = os.time() }`, :140) — in both branches without ever comparing `stored._lock.jobId` to `game.JobId`. There is no compare-and-swap, no abort-if-not-mine, no "someone else took this" telemetry. Verified live: `_lock` occurs at exactly 5 lines in the live MainGame module (91, 100, 118, 138, 140) and the live bytes for lines 96-148 are identical to the mirror.

All four write paths funnel through that unverified `trySave`: the left-while-loading hand-back (:238), PlayerRemoving (:279), the verdict/emote flush (:473), and BindToClose (:649). So an older server whose UpdateAsync is queued or delayed will, when it finally lands, (a) overwrite whatever the newer owner wrote, and (b) if it is a release, delete the newer owner's lock outright — leaving a live-owned profile with `_lock = nil`, loadable by any third server.

Two further source facts make the stale window reachable without inventing a crashed server:
1. The lock's `ts` is refreshed ONLY by a save (:140). There is no heartbeat/renew loop — grep for `_lock` finds no other writer. With `LOCK_STALE_SECONDS = 180` (:41) and flushes occurring only at the verdict (MachineFlow.luau:1325) or an emote grant (EmoteService.luau:260, :278), a profile that is genuinely owned and in play becomes stealable after 3 minutes without a verdict.
2. The menu place and MainGame share universe 10640788131 and the same KenopsiaProfile_v1 store (EmoteService.luau:471-472), and SoloExit teleports players out to the menu place — so MainGame server A -> menu -> MainGame server B is a first-class flow, and it is precisely the flow in which A's in-flight release can land after B has taken ownership.

Note on the mirror: Profiles is NOT mapped in default.project.json (per the prior parity pass), so the disk file is a hand-copy, not a Rojo artifact. I therefore confirmed the finding directly against the live place rather than relying on the mirror.

local lock = type(stored) == "table" and stored._lock or nil   -- [SOURCE] the ONLY read of _lock in the module, inside lockHeldByOther, called only from tryLoad
for _, k in ipairs(OWNED_FIELDS) do\n\t\t\t\tstored[k] = data[k]   -- [SOURCE] trySave overwrites every owned field with zero inspection of stored._lock
stored._lock = nil   -- [SOURCE] release branch: clears the lock unconditionally, even if it belongs to a different jobId
stored._lock = { jobId = game.JobId, ts = os.time() }   -- [SOURCE] non-release branch: stamps THIS server as owner unconditionally
return (now - (tonumber(lock.ts) or 0)) <= LOCK_STALE_SECONDS   -- [SOURCE] with LOCK_STALE_SECONDS = 180 (line 41): a lock older than 3 min is stealable
local ok, err = trySave(entry, true) -- write + hand the lock back   -- [SOURCE] PlayerRemoving path; one attempt, no retry, no ownership check
pcall(trySave, entry, true)   -- [SOURCE] BindToClose writes + releases every live entry unconditionally
local ok, err = trySave(entry, false)   -- [SOURCE] verdict/emote flush; re-stamps the lock, still no check
-- The CROSS-PLACE path. DEV and MainGame share universe 10640788131 and the KenopsiaProfile_v1 DataStore   -- [SOURCE] both places write the same keys

The live module is 663 lines, same as the mirror.

claims.playerImpact: Silent progression rollback and, in the worst ordering, two servers writing the same profile at once. Everything in OWNED_FIELDS (Profiles.luau:92-96) is exposed: xp, clearance, streak, sessions, roundsPlayed, viableCount, trialStats, quests, emotes, crates, settings. Concretely: a player finishes a session on MainGame server A, exits through the menu place (SoloExit teleport), and rejoins on server B; if A's release UpdateAsync is queued behind DataStore throttling and lands after B has stolen the (>180 s stale) lock, A's copy is written over B's and `_lock` is set to nil — the player loses whatever B had already banked, and the profile is left unlocked while B is still live, so a third server can load it concurrently and the next write wins arbitrarily. The player sees XP, a night streak, or a just-granted emote/crate disappear after a rejoin. A softer, more frequent variant is already reachable: if a release write fails outright, the orphaned lock blocks the next load for up to 180 s, the retry budget is only ~7 s (LOAD_ATTEMPTS 3, LOAD_BACKOFF {2,5}, lines 42-43), and the player then plays an entire session VOLATILE — nothing they earn is ever written (Profiles.luau:470 refuses to flush a volatile entry).
claims.runtimeNeeded: none - settled from source, and corroborated against the live place (weppy get_source of lines 96-148 plus a `_lock` search on game.ServerScriptService.KenopsiaServer.Services.Profiles, placeId 110672791536316). The absence of a check is a static property: `_lock` is read at exactly one line in the module and that line is not on the write path, so no runtime observation can make trySave verify ownership. If you want to observe the DAMAGE rather than the defect, the settling observation is: with two MainGame servers up, have one account leave server A and rejoin on server B while reading the raw KenopsiaProfile_v1 key `u_<userId>` through Open Cloud at each step — the bug is demonstrated the moment `_lock` reads nil (or carries A's JobId) while B holds a non-volatile live entry for that user, or the moment an OWNED_FIELDS value regresses to A's pre-leave value after B has already written a higher one. Note that this requires forcing the throttle/latency window, so a single clean rejoin will usually look fine; the defect is a race, not a deterministic failure.
claims.fixSketch: Make the token per-load and make every write compare-and-swap on it. At load, generate a fresh session token (HttpService:GenerateGUID(false)) and store `_lock = { jobId = game.JobId, token = <guid>, ts = now }`, keeping the guid on the live entry; keep the existing stale-steal rule for acquisition, since it is what rescues a genuinely crashed server. Then give trySave the check it is missing: inside its UpdateAsync transform, read `stored._lock` first and, if it exists and its `token` is not this entry's token, return nil to cancel the write (and surface it — a Telemetry event, not a silent drop) rather than clobbering the newer owner; only when the token matches should it copy OWNED_FIELDS and then either nil the lock (release) or re-stamp `ts`. Because the transform can now legitimately refuse, trySave must report "not mine" distinctly from "DataStore error" so that onLeave and BindToClose do not treat a refused write as a retryable failure, and so flush leaves `entry.dirty` alone in that case. Two smaller things belong in the same change: refresh `_lock.ts` on a cheap periodic renew (or shorten the gap another way) so a live-owned profile does not become stealable after 180 s just because no verdict landed, and widen the load retry budget past ~7 s so a legitimately locked profile is not silently downgraded to a full VOLATILE session on the first contended rejoin.

claims.finding:
Both halves of the claim are false against current source.

HALF 1 — "the main-menu place writes the same profile as MainGame". The menu place writes NO profile at all. [SOURCE] A repo-wide `grep -rl DataStoreService --include=*.luau` returns exactly two files: globalTypes.d.luau (a type stub) and studio-src/ServerScriptService/KenopsiaServer/Services/Profiles.luau. Zero hits anywhere under dev-src/. The store name "KenopsiaProfile_v1" appears only in studio-src (Profiles.luau:39 and three comments in EmoteService.luau). dev-src's only persistence API is MemoryStoreService — a different service and a different namespace ("KenopsiaRooms_v1", GameConfig.luau:35-37) — and even that is dead code: dev-src/ServerScriptService/KenopsiaServer/Main.server.luau requires only RoomService, PlaylistService and MenuPresenceService, never PartyRegistry, and dev-src RoomService.luau:3 states the omission is deliberate. dev-src/StarterPlayer/.../UI/Theme.luau:120 says outright "No DataStore in the MVP by design". [RUNTIME] In the live MainGame place (weppy, placeId 110672791536316), a game-wide search over 115 scripts finds DataStoreService in exactly one script (Profiles, lines 32 and 621) and MemoryStoreService in zero. So KenopsiaProfile_v1 has exactly ONE writer in the entire project, and it is in MainGame.

HALF 2 — "with no coordination between them". Three coordination mechanisms exist. (a) Profiles.luau:99-124 and 138-140 implement a per-key {jobId, ts} session lock with a 180 s stale-steal window that cancels the write and keeps the other server's lock — this is precisely the concurrent-write guard the claim asserts is absent, and because it is key-scoped it would apply across places as well as across servers. (b) A TeleportService handoff runs in both directions: dev-src PlaylistService.luau:166-169 does ReserveServer + TeleportAsync into MAIN_PLACE_ID 110672791536316, and studio-src SoloExit.luau:57,104 teleports back to MENU_PLACE_ID 129909297895850 ([RUNTIME] confirmed live at SoloExit:57). (c) A MessagingService topic "KenopsiaGrant_v1" is written and documented explicitly as "The CROSS-PLACE path" (EmoteService.luau:89, 290, 470-475, 479; [RUNTIME] present live at EmoteService:89).

SEPARATE FINDING, in the opposite direction from the claim: that cross-place path is HALF-BUILT. EmoteService.luau:283-284 asserts "DEV's crate ceremony calls this after it has written the durable grant" — no such caller exists. dev-src has no EmoteService, no MessagingService reference, no crate ceremony and no durable write. MainGame is both the publisher and the subscriber of its own topic ([RUNTIME] KenopsiaGrant_v1: 1 hit across all 115 live scripts, in MainGame's own EmoteService). The comment describes an intended DEV-side contract that is not implemented.

GRAIN OF TRUTH the claim may have been reaching for: no player state travels between the places. dev-src sets only opts.ReservedServerAccessCode and never SetTeleportData, and studio-src has ZERO hits for GetJoinData, JoinData, ReservedServerAccessCode, SetTeleportData or ReserveServer. So the menu hands players over with no payload and MainGame reads no join context. That is "no state handoff" — a very different statement from "both places write the same profile".

claims.playerImpact: Today, none of the corruption risk the claim implies. Because the menu place writes nothing, there is no double-writer on KenopsiaProfile_v1 and no cross-place clobber can occur; and even if there were a second writer, Profiles' {jobId, ts} lock (180 s stale window) is the guard that would arbitrate it. The actual player-visible consequence runs the other way: progression is invisible in the menu. A player who earns XP, clearance, streak or emotes in MainGame sees none of it in the main menu — the menu has no profile read path at all, and dev-src Theme.luau:120 says even local settings reset on leave. And the documented "crate ceremony in DEV publishes here and the player sees the emote without a rejoin" (EmoteService:471-473) cannot happen, because the DEV publisher half was never written; a crate opened in the menu would grant nothing anywhere. Note the reverse leg does work: a solo player left in MainGame is teleported back to the menu (SoloExit), so players do move between places — they just carry no state with them.
claims.fixSketch: Not to be implemented now. The gap is not "stop the menu writing profiles" (it does not write) but "the menu has no profile at all". The cheapest coherent shape is to make Profiles a shared module rather than a MainGame-only service: move it (and ProgressionRules, which it already depends on and which is pure) into the shared ReplicatedStorage/Kenopsia tree mapped by BOTH default.project.json and kenopsia-dev.project.json, then have the menu place start it in READ-MOSTLY mode — load on join under the same `_lock`, render clearance/XP/emote wheel, and release the lock immediately rather than holding it, so a player who then teleports into MainGame is not blocked by a lock their own menu server still holds. That lock-handoff at the teleport boundary is the one genuinely new piece of design: SoloExit and PlaylistService currently move players with no payload, and the safest ordering is menu-releases-before-TeleportAsync with MainGame's existing 180 s stale-steal as the backstop if the release call fails. Separately and independently, either implement the DEV crate ceremony that EmoteService:283 claims calls publishGrant, or delete that comment and the publisher half so the codebase stops documenting a caller that does not exist. Before any of this, fix the mirror hygiene it depends on: Profiles, EmoteService, Telemetry, SoloExit, Badges and Lobby are on disk but absent from default.project.json's Services block, so Rojo neither pushes nor pulls them and nothing would keep a shared Profiles in step across the two project files.

claims.finding:
I read the LIVE script off the connected datamodel (weppy clientId ad22f53b, placeId 110672791536316), not the stale mirror. Live `game.ReplicatedFirst.KenopsiaLoading` is 286 raw / 285 real lines vs the mirror's 163; the +122 lines are ALL cosmetic (grid rails, chamfered BootPanel, a `layout()` reflow). The teardown logic at live 242-284 is otherwise identical to the mirror, so both halves of the claim can be judged on live source.

TRUE — the unbounded parts:
(1) NO WATCHDOG EXISTS. A place-wide search across 115 live scripts for "KenopsiaLoading" returned 4 hits: two inside the file itself (:22, :276) and two inside a ServerStorage backup copy. Nothing else in the place ever touches `KenopsiaLoadingGui`. The single code path that removes it is `gui:Destroy()` at live:283, the last statement of ONE `task.spawn(function()` at live:242 that has NO pcall around its body. The GUI is an opaque full-screen cover (`bg.BackgroundColor3 = INK` at default transparency, `DisplayOrder = 100`, `ResetOnSpawn = false`). So any error thrown on an unprotected line inside that coroutine — e.g. live:253 `machineGui.Enabled = true` — kills the coroutine, `gui:Destroy()` is never reached, and the client is bricked behind a permanent black screen that respawning cannot clear. That is a genuinely unbounded failure mode with zero recovery.
(2) TWO UNBOUNDED YIELDS. `game.Loaded:Wait()` (live:245) has no timeout. `ContentProvider:PreloadAsync(criticalAssets)` (live:274) has no timeout — and the pcall at live:273-275 catches ERRORS, not YIELDS, so it imposes no time bound whatsoever. Both sit upstream of `gui:Destroy()`.
(3) AUDIO IS IN THE CRITICAL BATCH AND IS UPSTREAM OF TEARDOWN. Live:269-271 add `Music.Loop`, `SFX.Warning`, `SFX.Click`, and [RUNTIME] all three carry real asset ids (rbxassetid://136345765095808, //93861370808858, //71275573444924). `Music.Loop` is a background music loop and `SFX.Click` is a UI click — neither is needed to paint the first screen, so "nonessential" is a fair description. A stalled audio fetch does hold the loading screen, with no ceiling written anywhere in the code.

FALSE / OVERSTATED — the bounded parts the claim denies:
(1) "no bounded failure/recovery path" is too absolute. Three of the four failure modes DO have correct, bounded recovery. `playerGui:WaitForChild("KenopsiaMachine", 20)` (live:251) is timeout-bounded and nil-guarded by `if machineGui then` (live:252) — on failure it skips the whole block and still falls through to `gui:Destroy()`. `machineGui:WaitForChild("Warning", 10)` (live:254) is bounded and nil-guarded at live:255. PreloadAsync errors are caught and warned at live:273-276 and execution continues. On all three of those failures the screen DOES come down.
(2) "indefinitely" is not provable from source. The engine may impose its own per-request timeouts inside PreloadAsync. What source proves is "unbounded by this code", not "infinite in practice".
(3) One preload target is dead: live:268 `add(music and music:FindFirstChild("Intro"))` — [RUNTIME] `find_child(game.SoundService.KenopsiaAudio.Music, "Intro")` returns `{"found": false}`. Music.Intro does not exist; that add contributes nothing. Only 3 sounds + GrungeWash actually preload.

NEW FINDING the claim missed, and it is larger than the hazard the claim focuses on: live:254 `machineGui:WaitForChild("Warning", 10)` ALWAYS burns the full 10 seconds. No `Warning` GUI object exists anywhere in the place (verify1/live-gui.md confirms it three independent ways), and MachineLayout only READS it (lines 34/410/492/651, all guarded `FindFirstChild`) — nothing creates it at runtime. So every single join eats a deterministic 10 s stall that sits BEFORE the preload block even begins. That is bounded, but it is the biggest guaranteed contributor to load time, whereas the audio hazard is speculative.

FORWARD-LOOKING HAZARD: `default.project.json:9` maps `KenopsiaLoading` to the mirror file, so a Rojo sync WOULD overwrite live. The mirror (studio-src/...:133-143) contains an extra block live lacks, adding every `ImageLabel` under `KenopsiaMenu.Root` to the same batch. Syncing would enlarge the unbounded preload set and make the hazard strictly worse.

claims.finding:
Three of the four sub-claims are true as stated; the fourth is true in mechanism but materially overstated in consequence. First, a parity note that removes the stated hazard for this claim: Services/Profiles is NOT mapped in default.project.json, so the mirror is not a Rojo artifact — but I read the LIVE MainGame source (placeId 110672791536316, weppy clientId ad22f53b, studioState "edit") for every region I quote below (lines 39-45, 126-150, 272-284, 465-480, 636-663) and it is byte-identical to studio-src. So this finding is [RUNTIME]-backed, not mirror-only.

(1) "No budget-aware periodic autosave" — CONFIRMED, and it is deliberate, not an oversight. There is no timer, no Heartbeat loop, no task.delay anywhere in Profiles; writes happen only at discrete trigger points. [RUNTIME] a live search of game.ServerScriptService (34 scripts) for "RequestBudget" returned 0 matches, and "UpdateAsync" returned matches in exactly one writer, Profiles (lines 110 and 132) — nothing in the whole server ever consults DataStore budget. Two qualifiers the handoff omits: the file's own header declares this ("writes at EXACTLY three moments", line 15; "a dirty profile that never flushes is lost by design", line 26), and at a 4-player cap the write budget (60 + 10*players per minute) is never remotely approached by a handful of writes per session, so the missing budget-awareness carries no practical throttling risk here. The real exposure of having no autosave is narrower than "no autosave" sounds: a hard crash (BindToClose does not run) loses at most the progress since the last verdict flush.

Also, the header's "EXACTLY three moments" is now stale: EmoteService adds two more Profiles.flush call sites (lines 260 and 278), so there are five write triggers, not three.

(2) "Saves are not serialized per player" — CONFIRMED. trySave (line 129) has no mutex, no in-flight flag, no queue; the entry table (line 55) carries no such field. Four independent callers can enter trySave for the SAME userId/key concurrently: Profiles.flush's spawned thread (471-473), onLeave on the PlayerRemoving thread (279), each BindToClose spawned thread (647-649), and the loader's left-while-loading path (238). Worse, flush's `not entry.dirty` early-out (470) is NOT an in-flight guard, because dirty is only cleared after UpdateAsync returns (145) — so two flush calls inside one write round-trip (e.g. EmoteService.grant twice, or the verdict flush at MachineFlow:1325 followed by an emote grant) each spawn their own concurrent UpdateAsync on the same key. EmoteService:266 shows the author is aware same-key writes are throttled, yet no serialization was added.

(3) "An older in-flight save can complete after the final release" — CONFIRMED at the code level; its store-level outcome needs runtime. The window is concrete and is the exact scenario MachineFlow already anticipates ("after scoresCommitted, before the presentation holds a quitter can cancel", MachineFlow:1288-1289): verdict fires Profiles.flush -> spawned thread passes its `live[entry.userId] ~= entry` guard (472) -> trySave(entry, false) yields inside UpdateAsync -> the player quits -> onLeave nils the live slot and calls trySave(entry, true) (279), a second UpdateAsync on the same key. The guard at 472 runs BEFORE the yield, so it cannot catch this. The two writes differ only in the lock branch (137-141): release writes `stored._lock = nil`, the non-release flush writes `_lock = { jobId = game.JobId, ts = os.time() }`. Nothing in the code orders them. Note a precision point the handoff gets wrong by implication: the late flush would NOT write stale field values, because trySave captures entry.data by REFERENCE (130) and reads data[k] inside the transform (135), so it serializes whatever the live table holds at transform time. The only thing that can land stale is the LOCK.

(4) "No mutation tracking, so a completed save can clear newer unsaved changes" — PARTIAL. The mechanism is exactly as described: state is a single boolean `dirty`, there is no version/mutation counter, and `entry.dirty = false` is set after UpdateAsync returns (145), so any mutation landing between the transform returning and the call returning is marked clean without having been written. But the stated consequence is overstated. `dirty` gates ONE path only — Profiles.flush (470). onLeave (277: `if not entry or entry.volatile or not store then return end`) and BindToClose (645: `if not entry.volatile then`) both save unconditionally, with no dirty check. So a wrongly-cleared flag suppresses an intermediate flush, not the final write; actual data loss additionally requires the server to die without BindToClose running. "Newer unsaved changes get cleared" is true of the flag, not of the durable outcome on a normal leave or shutdown.

claims.playerImpact: The one path with real player-visible cost is (3), and it is a lock leak, not corrupted stats. If the verdict flush commits after onLeave's release, the key is left holding `_lock = {jobId = <the server they just left>, ts = <flush time>}`. lockHeldByOther (line 102) exempts only the SAME JobId, so a rejoin to a DIFFERENT server inside 180 s (LOCK_STALE_SECONDS, line 41) is blocked. tryLoad then burns LOAD_ATTEMPTS = 3 with LOAD_BACKOFF {2, 5} — about 7 s total — and gives up, leaving the player VOLATILE for that entire session (header line 11: "when every try fails the player simply stays VOLATILE"). A volatile entry is never written back (onLeave line 277 returns early on entry.volatile), so that whole session's XP, streak, quests and crate keys are silently discarded, with no player-facing signal. claims.finding:
Two of the three sub-claims are CONFIRMED from source; the framing word "undefined" is REFUTED.

(1) REFUTED — "Loading failure and slow load are undefined." Server-side they are precisely defined, deliberate and documented. Profiles.luau seeds every joiner with a volatile in-memory ProgressionRules.defaultProfile() before any DataStore call (:218-225), then retries the load LOAD_ATTEMPTS=3 times with LOAD_BACKOFF {2,5} s (:42-43, :229-254). If every attempt fails the player simply stays volatile: fully playable, nothing ever written (:11-12). Every write path guards on it — Profiles.flush returns false when entry.volatile (:470), onLeave returns early (:277), BindToClose skips volatile entries (:645). This is an explicit, tested design, not an undefined state.

(2) CONFIRMED — "progress earned during loading is silently replaced when the stored profile arrives." Profiles.luau:244 is an unconditional whole-table replacement, `entry.data = data`, with no merge of the volatile table, no diff, no warn, no telemetry, no packet. Every mutation any writer made to entry.data between :225 (entry published into `live`) and :244 is discarded. There is no volatile guard on ANY writer: recordSession (:316), recordTrial (:442), grantEmote (:544), setEquipped (:565), setEmoteSlot (:578), setWheel (:598) all mutate entry.data freely while the load is in flight, and the only thing that would have persisted them — Profiles.flush — silently no-ops for a volatile entry (:470) and its `false` return is discarded by both callers (MachineFlow.luau:1325 and EmoteService.luau:260/278 both use bare `pcall(Profiles.flush, ...)`). The same wholesale discard happens on the left-while-loading branch (:235 `entry.data = data`, then :238 `trySave(entry, true)` writes the STORE copy back, not the accumulated one). The exposure window is one task.spawn resumption plus UpdateAsync latency at minimum, and widens to 7 s + latency whenever attempts 1-2 fail (throttle/outage) — exactly the "slow load" case. Note :246 then sets entry.dirty = true regardless, so not even the dirty flag carries a signal that anything was lost.

(3) CONFIRMED — "'progress cannot be saved' is never made visible to the player." The server DOES compute the flag and DOES send it — twice — but both packets land on client kinds that nothing dispatches. Profiles.luau:184 puts `volatile = entry.volatile` inside a `kind = "profilestate"` packet; grep of the ENTIRE repo (studio-src + dev-src) finds "profilestate" exactly once — the sender at :178. There is no consumer. The file's own comment at :171-172 says so: "The UI contract, dark until a later phase renders it: an unknown kind renders NOTHING on the client". The second carrier, receipt.volatile -> MachineFlow.luau:1365 inside `kind = "shiftreport"`, is dark by the author's own admission at MachineFlow.luau:1336-1337. Everything else pushes the other way: sendGreeting explicitly returns for a volatile profile (:197, comment :195 "a volatile load stays silent"), so a player whose progress cannot be saved gets LESS feedback than one whose can. The only failure surface is a server-console warn (:249, :256, :281, :475, :625) — and warnOnce is keyed on a module-scope `warned` table (:53, :58-60) with a single global key "load", so after the FIRST player's failed load every subsequent player's failure is silent even in the server log. Telemetry.funnel goes to AnalyticsService only (Telemetry.luau:100-104), never to a client.

Highest-impact instance of (3), worth separating: tryLoad returns blocked with err "locked by another server" when another server's session lock is younger than LOCK_STALE_SECONDS=180 (:99-104, :124). Three blocked attempts leave the player volatile for the WHOLE session — every verdict, XP grant, streak tick and quest completion accumulates into a table that is never written and is dropped at PlayerRemoving — with zero player-facing indication. That is a rejoin-after-a-server-crash scenario, not a hypothetical.

First, make the load landing a merge rather than an assignment: at Profiles.luau:244 the volatile table is the newer authority for anything a writer touched, so track a per-entry `touched` flag (set it in the same places that already set entry.dirty) and, when it is set, either fold the volatile deltas into the loaded table field-by-field or — far simpler and probably correct for this codebase — refuse the replacement and keep playing volatile with a warn plus a Telemetry.event, since silently discarding earned progress is strictly worse than declining a stale load. Second, close the honesty gap on the write path: Profiles.flush already returns false for a volatile entry but both call sites throw the answer away, so give recordSession's receipt an explicit `unsaved = true` and have MachineFlow surface it. claims.finding:
Both halves of the claim are false today.

HALF 1 -- "cancellation reported as MINIGAME ERROR": there are exactly two `abort()` call sites in the entire server, both in MachineFlow's finalizer, and neither is the cancellation route. `RoomServiceRef.abort(room, "MINIGAME ERROR")` fires only for `outcome == "error"` (MachineFlow.luau:1395-1398) and `"NO READY MINIGAME"` only for `outcome == "no-trial"` (:1399-1400). A player leaving takes a completely different path: RoomService.removeMember calls `abortMatch("PLAYER LEFT - CANNOT CONTINUE WITH A SINGLE PLAYER")` (RoomService.luau:340), which fires `fail(plr, "RUN ABORTED - " .. string.upper(reason))` to every player (:248) on the LobbyError remote, and AbortScreen renders that exact string on a full-screen black card (AbortScreen.client.luau:92-95). The player reads "RUN ABORTED - PLAYER LEFT - CANNOT CONTINUE WITH A SINGLE PLAYER".

There IS a real but log-only mislabel behind the claim. When the abort lands while a round thread is running, runRoundGuarded returns `false, "aborted"` (MachineFlow:782); the trial loop treats anything that is not `"timeout"` as fatal and re-raises it (`error(rScores, 0)`, :1111 and :1118), so the xpcall fails and the finalizer sets `outcome = "error"` (:1384-1385) rather than `"cancelled"`. That produces `warn("[MachineFlow] session <id> failed: aborted")` and `print("[RoomService] cleanup (error)")`. It does NOT reach players: the follow-up `abort(room, "MINIGAME ERROR")` hits abortMatch's two re-entry guards -- `if room.phase ~= "Playing" and room.phase ~= "Starting" then return false end` (phase is already "Aborting") and `if room.aborting then return false end` -- and returns false without sending a second LobbyError (RoomService.luau:240-241). `outcome` has no consumer other than those two branches and the cleanup print (grep: MachineFlow:1395, :1399, :1405), so nothing else is corrupted by the mislabel.

HALF 2 -- "cleanup is not idempotent": refuted at every layer I checked. MachineFlow's per-match `cleanup()` is latched (`if cleaned then return end; cleaned = true`, :802-803). RoomService.cleanupToWaiting is explicitly documented and guarded ("Idempotent: safe to call from a finally-style path and again from the watchdog", :226-229). abortMatch is guarded twice (:240-241). TrialKit's `Round:cleanup()` latches on `self.cleaned` (:807-809). CanteenProtocol's `cleanupRound(st)` latches on `st.cleaned` and nils `current` (:936-940), which matters because the abort route calls the trial's `abort()` hook from runRoundGuarded (:778-781) and then the trial's `cleanup()` hook from the finalizer -- the second call is a no-op. BirdHunting.abort, Minefield.abort and CanteenProtocol.abort all nil `_guard` before running `g.cleanup`, so a repeat abort does nothing.

PARITY NOTE: this finding does not rest on the drifted mirror. I re-read every quoted region out of the live MainGame datamodel via the weppy bridge (placeId 110672791536316, clientId ad22f53b, alias studio-2) -- MachineFlow 766-784 / 800-812 / 1107-1121 / 1382-1406, RoomService 226-252 / 319-346, AbortScreen 86-97 -- and all of it is byte-identical to studio-src. KenopsiaClient's own LobbyError handler (:3150-3169) is only the small amber notice line and is a mirror read, so its live wording is unconfirmed -- but it is additive and cannot turn "PLAYER LEFT" into "MINIGAME ERROR".

claims.finding:
Two halves, and they need separating.

TRUE (mechanism): the hunter scheduler does always start at roster slot 1, every session. The seat is chosen in MachineFlow, not in BirdHunting. The trial loop is `for roundIndex = 1, rounds do` (MachineFlow:1002) and the seat is `room.members[(roundIndex - 1) % #room.members + 1]` (MachineFlow:1023). roundIndex 1 therefore always resolves to index 1. There is no per-session offset, no carried cursor, and no member shuffle — the session `seed` in MachineFlow shuffles the TRIAL ORDER only (MachineFlow:10 "played once each, in a seed-shuffled order"), never `room.members`. [RUNTIME] the same expression is present in the live MainGame place at the identical line 1023 (weppy get/search against clientId ad22f53b, placeId 110672791536316), so this is not a stale-mirror artifact.

MISLEADING (the stated cause): "starts at member one" is not what denies anybody the role. The denial comes from leg count < roster size. `Pacing.roundsFor("birdhunt", n)` returns `row(LEGS, n)` with `LEGS = { [2] = 3, [3] = 3, [4] = 3 }` (Pacing.luau:60) — three legs at EVERY player count. [RUNTIME] confirmed live: Pacing:60 in the place reads `local LEGS = { [2] = 3, [3] = 3, [4] = 3 }`. The offline proof pins it too: tests/rules.lua:50 asserts birdhunt 4p -> 3.

So the actual behaviour, per roster size (MaxPlayers = 4, GameConfig.luau:21):
  * 4 players -> 3 legs -> hunters are members[1], [2], [3]. **members[4] never hunts.** Claim's consequence holds, but ONLY here.
  * 3 players -> 3 legs -> members[1], [2], [3]. Everyone hunts exactly once. Nobody is denied.
  * 2 players -> 3 legs -> members[1], [2], [1]. Nobody is denied; the asymmetry runs the OTHER way — slot 1 hunts twice.
  * 1 player -> `if isBird and #room.members >= 2` (MachineFlow:1022) is false, so no hunter card and no forced hunter at all.

"Across sessions" also holds, and for a reason the handoff did not state: `room.members` is append-ordered by join (`table.insert(room.members, {...})`, RoomService.luau:172) and is NOT cleared when a match ends — the return-to-Waiting path resets only ready flags and progress fields, then `promoteSpectators()` APPENDS (RoomService.luau:221). So in a server that keeps its four players, the 4th-joined player is the denied slot in every consecutive Bird Hunting trial.

Also worth flagging, because it is almost certainly what produced this handoff: two comments in the shipping source still assert the OLD leg counts under which nobody would be denied — MachineFlow:1102 "(2p 4 / 3p 3 / 4p 4), so this is no longer 5 x playerCount" and Pacing.luau:54-55 "3-player sessions run 3 and 4-player sessions run 4". Both were invalidated by the 22.08.2026 P0.3 change three lines below the Pacing one. Read the comments and 4p looks safe; read the code and it is not.

One more thing the claim gets wrong by omission: BirdHunting's own rotation (BirdHunting.luau:481, live-confirmed at the same line) is dead on the session path. It fires only when `forcedHunterUserId` is nil, which the comment at :478-480 says "only happens on a direct or solo test call". When the scheduled hunter has left, the leg is SKIPPED, not reassigned (:463-476, "SKIPPED, NEVER SUBSTITUTED").

claims.finding:
The mechanism the claim describes is real, but two of its words are wrong.

TRUE (confirmed on disk AND in the live place): "Joined" is emitted from inside the spawned profile-load thread in Profiles.onPlayer, after the whole DataStore load loop has finished, and it sits behind a liveness guard. Profiles.luau:227 opens `task.spawn(function()`; :229-254 is the `for attempt = 1, LOAD_ATTEMPTS` load/backoff loop; :258 is `if live[userId] ~= entry or plr.Parent ~= Players then return end`; :261 is `Telemetry.funnel(plr, FUNNEL, 1, "Joined")`. Two further returns inside the loop (:232 on a load that succeeded after the player left, :252 during backoff) also skip it. onLeave nils `live[plr.UserId]` at :276, so the moment PlayerRemoving fires, every one of those guards trips. A player who leaves before the load thread reaches :261 therefore never enters the funnel at all — not even at step 1, the funnel's first step. This is the ONLY join-side analytics call in the game: a game-wide live search of 115 scripts found exactly one `Telemetry.funnel(..., 1, "Joined")` (Profiles:261) and exactly one `AnalyticsService` consumer (Telemetry).

WRONG #1 — terminology: it is not a custom "Joined" *event*. It is funnel step 1 of the funnel `KenopsiaRetention` (Profiles.luau:45 `local FUNNEL = "KenopsiaRetention"`), routed to `AnalyticsService:LogFunnelStepEvent` (Telemetry.luau:104), not to `LogCustomEvent`. Nothing named "Joined" reaches the custom-event stream. Roblox's own engine-side join/session/DAU analytics are untouched by any of this, so early exits are hidden only from THIS funnel, not from analytics generally.

WRONG #2 — causality: a FAILED load does not suppress "Joined". When all three attempts fail, the `for` loop simply ends, execution falls through to the :258 guard, and — if the player is still there — the funnel step fires anyway on the volatile profile. Failure suppresses nothing by itself; it only widens the window. LOAD_ATTEMPTS = 3 with LOAD_BACKOFF = { 2, 5 } (Profiles.luau:42-43) means a fully failing load blocks the fire for at least 7 s of `task.wait` plus three UpdateAsync round trips, versus a few hundred ms on the happy path. So the accurate statement is: load LATENCY (which failure maximises) is the suppression window; a successful-but-slow load hides an exit exactly as well as a failed one, and a failed load with the player still present is fully counted.

Sharpest form of the real problem: the ~7 s failure window coincides almost exactly with the content-warning hold that Profiles' own comment describes — "The boot watchdog holds joiners out for 7 s while the content warning plays" (Profiles.luau:46-47) — i.e. precisely the moment a player is most likely to quit. When the DataStore is healthy, quits during the content warning ARE counted (the load resolves in well under a second). When it is degraded, they silently are not.

Extra defect found while verifying, outside the claim: step 2 is not gated on the load thread. MachineFlow.luau:474-476 fires `Telemetry.funnel(plr, "KenopsiaRetention", 2, "RouletteSeen")` straight off room membership. A player still stuck in the 7 s retry path can therefore be logged at step 2 before step 1, producing out-of-order funnel steps on top of the missing ones.

Live-vs-mirror status for this finding: NOT dependent on the stale client scripts. Both files are server-side, and I read the live place directly — live Profiles:212-270 and :39-49 came back byte-identical to the mirror, as did live Telemetry:100-109. Note however that live-parity.md records that Profiles and Telemetry are not mapped in default.project.json, so their agreement is manual, not tool-maintained.

claims.finding:
CONFIRMED, with one qualification the handoff omits: the mismatch is not hidden — LightGuard documents it in its own header.

WHAT THE CODE ACTUALLY DOES. LightGuard.client.luau is a single `task.delay(3, ...)` with no loop and no RenderStepped. Its entire gate is two conditions: (1) `UserInputService.TouchEnabled` (line 33 — desktop returns immediately), and (2) `UserGameSettings.SavedQualityLevel.Value <= 4` (lines 37/39, `LowQualityMax = 4` at line 19). If both hold it raises client-local `Lighting.Ambient`/`OutdoorAmbient` by (14,16,20)/255, sets the attribute `KenopsiaLowLight` (lines 52-54), and fires one RemoteEvent packet whose `event` field is the string `"MobileBlackScreen"` (line 63). Nothing in the file reads a frame, a pixel, a ViewportFrame, a screenshot, or any rendered output — Roblox exposes no such readback. So the claim's two substantive halves are both true: it IS a device/quality heuristic, and it is NOT black-image detection. The name-vs-measurement mismatch is therefore real.

The one payload field that sounds like a measurement, `texMB` (lines 42-48, `Stats:GetMemoryUsageMbForTag(GraphicsTexture)` bucketed to 25 MB steps), is reported only — it never gates the emit. Same for `touch` (line 66), which is structurally always `true` because line 33 already returned otherwise: a constant field in the payload.

QUALIFICATION — the naming is a deliberate, documented choice, not an accident. The file's own header states it in as many words: line 4 "Roblox has no pixel readback, so this is an honest heuristic", and lines 7-9 "report ONE diagnostic \"MobileBlackScreen\" telemetry event -- it fires on the heuristic, not on a proven black frame; the name is kept for the analytics counter." So if the handoff means "someone reading only the event name in an analytics dashboard will be misled" — true. If it implies an undiscovered defect or an author who did not know — false; the author named the mismatch and gave the reason (an existing analytics counter to keep continuous).

SOLE EMITTER, AND NO SERVER-SIDE VERIFICATION. LightGuard is the only producer of this event anywhere. Server-side, Telemetry.luau merely whitelists the name (line 28 `MobileBlackScreen = true,`), rate-limits it to 1 per player per 60 s, and forwards it verbatim to `AnalyticsService:LogCustomEvent` under that name (line 128) — it adds no corroborating check, so the dashboard counter carries the heuristic's meaning unmodified.

BEYOND THE CLAIM — the mismatch is wider than "not a black frame". Per the file's own comments (line 19 "Automatic (0) .. QualityLevel4"; line 40 "0 is Automatic, 1..4 the low tiers"), quality value 0 is Automatic, which is Roblox's default setting. A gate of `<= 4` therefore admits the default. If that mapping holds, every touch client on default settings that survives 3 s passes, and the counter approximates "mobile sessions alive at 3 s" rather than "at-risk clients" — let alone black screens. CAVEAT: I took the 0==Automatic numeric mapping from the file's comments; the local API dump (roblox.yml line 13072+) lists the SavedQualitySetting enum items but my grep did not surface their numeric values, so I did not confirm it independently. This sub-point is the one part of my analysis that is not fully nailed down.

claims.finding:
The claim is half wrong and half right, and the two halves must be separated.

HALF ONE - "clients are not shown exactly who is ready" - REFUTED. Every client is shown exactly who is ready, per seat, with a checkbox. The server ships the flag: RoomService.publicState() puts `ready` on every member of the RoomState packet [SOURCE studio-src RoomService.luau:104, byte-identical LIVE at RoomService:104 read through the weppy bridge]. The client paints it: `updateRoster()` walks four rows and sets `row.Check.Fill.Visible = m.ready == true` per seat, writing the display name for an occupied seat and the literal string "vacant" for an empty one [RUNTIME live KenopsiaClient:2487-2526, fetched verbatim from the connected place]. The GUI it paints into is really there - I enumerated it live: `Info.Roster.Row1..Row4`, each with `Check` (containing `Fill` and a `UIStroke`), `RankLabel`, `ScoreLabel`, `NameLabel`, 28 descendants in total [RUNTIME query_instances children game.StarterGui.KenopsiaMachine.Info.Roster]. The local player additionally gets their own state on the button itself - AMBER when ready, PHOSPHOR when seated-and-not-ready, DIM when benched [RUNTIME live KenopsiaClient:2457-2485]. And it stays current: `setReady` calls `broadcast()` on every toggle [SOURCE RoomService.luau:372], and the client's RoomState handler calls `updateRoster(p.members or {})` on every packet [RUNTIME live KenopsiaClient:2572]. This is NOT the stale-mirror hazard: the roster code is identical in the repo mirror (KenopsiaClient.client.luau:1988-2026) and in the live 4125-line script, so the drift does not touch it.

HALF TWO - "what is preventing a start" is not surfaced - CONFIRMED, and it is worse than the claim states, because the code that would explain it exists but is unreachable.

(a) The ONLY path that starts a match is `maybeAutoStart()`, and it returns silently on both blocking conditions - too few seated players, and not-all-ready - with no `fail()`, no packet, no log [SOURCE + RUNTIME RoomService:311-317, live source identical].

(b) The two strings that WOULD name the reason - "NOT ENOUGH PLAYERS" and "ALL PLAYERS MUST BE READY" - live inside the `RoomStartRequest` handler [SOURCE RoomService.luau:622-629]. Nothing fires that remote. A live search of the whole datamodel returned 2 hits across 115 scripts, both inside RoomService itself (the remote-name list at :568 and the handler at :616) [RUNTIME manage_scripts search path=game pattern=RoomStartRequest]. No client script fires it; KenopsiaClient contains zero occurrences of "StartRequest" [RUNTIME]. Those two messages are dead code. The only lobby rejections a player can actually receive are the ones `setReady` emits - "SPECTATING - NEXT MATCH" and "RUN IN PROGRESS" [SOURCE RoomService.luau:353,357] - rendered by the KenopsiaNotice overlay [RUNTIME live KenopsiaClient:3927-3987].

(c) The threshold itself is never sent. RoomState carries `maxPlayers` but no minimum [SOURCE RoomService.luau:118], and the client reads `maxPlayers = p.maxPlayers or 4` and nothing else of the kind [RUNTIME live KenopsiaClient:2541]. MinPlayers = 2, RequireAllReady = true [SOURCE GameConfig.luau:21-23]. So a lone ready player sees one filled checkbox and three rows saying "vacant" and has no way to learn from the UI that two are required.

(d) The client discards most of the packet. Its RoomState handler reads only `maxPlayers`, `members` and `spectators`; it never touches `phase`, `stage`, `countdown` or any of the eight progress fields [RUNTIME live KenopsiaClient:2539-2574]. In particular `room.countdown` is broadcast every second during the Starting phase [SOURCE RoomService.luau:117, 283-288] and is rendered nowhere - a live case-sensitive search for "countdown" in KenopsiaClient returns 2 hits, both comments [RUNTIME]. So the 3-second pre-match countdown (Config.Match.StartCountdown = 3) is invisible too.

(e) Ambient text that was written for exactly this moment ships dark. `MachineVoice.Lines.idle` holds ten authored lobby lines including "WAITING FOR A FULL SHIFT." and "SEATS AVAILABLE. VOLUNTEERS ARE NOT." [SOURCE MachineVoice.luau:94-104], but `MachineVoice.pick` is called exactly once in the entire server, for category "lastdiner" [SOURCE CanteenProtocol.luau:1281]. The "idle" pool has no consumer. The one line actually on screen is TopTicker's authored, never-recomputed text "Simulation bootstrapper completed. Waiting for subjects ..." [RUNTIME query_instances get Info.TopTicker], which the client only ever overwrites with the spectator notice [RUNTIME live KenopsiaClient:2567-2571].

So: consent state is fully legible; the blocking REASON is only inferable, and only for the not-all-ready case (you can see whose checkbox is empty). For the below-minimum case there is no signal at all beyond three rows reading "vacant".

claims.playerImpact:
Two different experiences, and only one of them is broken.

Seeing who is ready works. Once the lobby Info panel is up, every player sees a four-row roster: each occupied seat shows a display name and a checkbox that fills the instant that player readies, and empty seats read "vacant" in dim. claims.finding:
The claim's first half is CONFIRMED and in fact understated; its second half is REFUTED.

TRUE (understated). `RematchAccepted` is fired on nothing a player does. At the verdict, MachineFlow arms `room.rematch.userIds` from `ctx.participantUserIds` — every participant of the session that just ended, unconditionally, with no input consulted ([SOURCE] MachineFlow.luau:1279-1281). ~7 s after the room returns to Waiting (0.4 s at :1407 plus `Pacing.Timing.LobbyReveal` 6.4 s at :479), preFlow fires the funnel for every one of those userIds still present in `room.members` ([SOURCE] MachineFlow.luau:499-508). The 60 s window at :501 never expires (elapsed is ~18 s). No button press is required, checked, or recorded. The authors state the intent plainly in German at :496-498 — "whoever stayed seated after the verdict counts as rematch interest" — so this is a knowing presence-proxy shipped under a step name that says "Accepted".

STRONGER THAN CLAIMED: there is no opt-out at all, so this is not merely "leaving without accepting can count" — everyone counts.
(1) The one clearing path is `setReady(player, false)` → `rematch.userIds[player.UserId] = nil` ([SOURCE] RoomService.luau:365-367), but `setReady` is phase-gated to Waiting/Starting ([SOURCE] RoomService.luau:356-359). The results screen runs while the room is still Playing: the final board goes out at MachineFlow:1271, then `hold(ctx, Pacing.Timing.FinalScore)` = 6.0 s (:1330, Pacing.luau:150), then the shift-report packet, then `hold(ctx, Pacing.Timing.ShiftReport or 5.0)` = 5.0 s (:1371, Pacing.luau:182), and only then `cleanupToWaiting` at :1405. For those ~11 s any un-ready is rejected with "RUN IN PROGRESS" and the set is untouched.
(2) The "BACK TO MENU" button that is supposed to un-ready ([SOURCE] KenopsiaClient.client.luau:3245, :3268 → `dismiss(false)` → `ReadyRemote:FireServer(ready)` at :3227) lives on an end card that is only shown on a `podium` CLEAR packet ([SOURCE] :3295-3301). No server code ever sends `kind = "podium"`: `Podium.raise`/`Podium.strike` have zero callers in studio-src — the only hits are in the abandoned worktree `.claude/worktrees/mp-08-death-and-spectate/`. MachineFlow:1373 says so outright ("DER PODIUMS-BEAT IST RAUS"). The opt-out UI therefore never appears.
(3) You cannot leave the seat either: `RoomLeaveRequest` is a deliberate no-op ([SOURCE] RoomService.luau:606-611) and `removeMember` is called only from `Players.PlayerRemoving` ([SOURCE] RoomService.luau:633-634). The sole way to avoid the event is to quit the Roblox game within ~18 s of the verdict.

FALSE. "can count as a replay" is wrong. `RematchAccepted` has zero gameplay effect — `Telemetry.funnel` does nothing but `AnalyticsService:LogFunnelStepEvent` ([SOURCE] Telemetry.luau:100-109). It readies nobody and starts no match. The auto-rematch that used to ride on this same set was deleted on 30.08.2026 ([SOURCE] MachineFlow.luau:490-498), and `RoomService.carryReady` ([SOURCE] RoomService.luau:379) is now dead code with zero callers in studio-src or dev-src. So nothing is replayed; only the metric is wrong.

NET: a telemetry-integrity defect, not a gameplay defect. Step 5 of the KenopsiaRetention funnel measures "did not quit within ~18 s of the verdict", not "chose to play again", and will read near-100 % conversion from step 4 (VerdictSeen, MachineFlow:1327), making the funnel's last step uninformative. `Telemetry.funnel` also passes `funnelSessionId = nil` (:104), so the "Analytics dedupes repeats per player" assumption asserted in the comment at MachineFlow:472-473 is itself unverified.

TRUE (confirmed in the repo AND in the live MainGame place): there is exactly ONE funnel name in the entire game, "KenopsiaRetention", and every one of its steps is logged through AnalyticsService:LogFunnelStepEvent with funnelSessionId explicitly nil. [SOURCE] studio-src/.../Services/Telemetry.luau:104 `AnalyticsService:LogFunnelStepEvent(player, funnelName, nil, step, stepName)`. [RUNTIME] I read the same line back from the live datamodel (weppy bridge, clientId ad22f53b..., placeId 110672791536316, studioState "edit"): live Telemetry line 104 is byte-identical, and a place-wide search of all 115 live scripts returns exactly 5 Telemetry.funnel call sites at the same line numbers as the mirror. Telemetry.luau, MachineFlow.luau and Profiles.luau are server modules and are NOT in the known client-drift set, so the mirror is trustworthy here — and I confirmed it live anyway.

TRUE: steps 2-5 are per-MATCH and genuinely recur inside one server. Step 2 RouletteSeen fires in preFlow, and preFlow is re-spawned after every match (MachineFlow.luau:1408-1410, `if room.phase == "Waiting" and #room.members > 0 then room.preShown = true; task.spawn(preFlow, room)`). Step 3 Round1Done is gated on `trialIndex == 1 and roundIndex == 1`, which resets on every runMatch. Step 4 VerdictSeen fires per verdict, step 5 RematchAccepted per rematch window. So a player who plays three matches on one server emits RouletteSeen/Round1Done/VerdictSeen three times each, all indistinguishable.

TRUE: this is the wrong API for the intent. Roblox's own funnel docs (create.roblox.com/docs/production/analytics/funnel-events) split funnels in two: an onboarding funnel tracks "conversion events that only occur once per user" and uses LogOnboardingFunnelStepEvent(); a session funnel tracks "conversion events that occur multiple times per user" and uses LogFunnelStepEvent(), where funnelSessionId exists "to distinguish between different sessions of the same user in a recurring funnel". The code calls the SESSION api with the session key omitted. LogOnboardingFunnelStepEvent exists in the API surface (globalTypes.d.luau:9233) and is never called anywhere in the repo or the live place.

TRUE: the code's own comments state the opposite assumption as fact and it is unverified. MachineFlow.luau:473-474 asserts "One-time funnel -- Analytics dedupes repeats per player." Nothing in the Roblox funnel docs promises per-player dedup for LogFunnelStepEvent — that promise belongs to the onboarding variant. Either branch breaks reconciliation: if the engine does dedupe, only a player's first match per lifetime is ever counted and per-match conversion is unmeasurable; if it does not, steps 2-5 accumulate N times per single step-1 event and step-to-step conversion exceeds 100%. Neither number equals the count of real matches.

FALSE / IMPRECISE: "mixed with one-time onboarding steps". No step in this funnel is one-time. Step 1 "Joined" fires on EVERY server join (Profiles.luau:261, inside the onJoin profile-load path), not once per user lifetime, and it does not use the onboarding API. The actual cadence mixture inside the single funnel name is per-JOIN (step 1) versus per-MATCH (steps 2-5) — still a real defect, and still the reason the funnel is unreconcilable, but the handoff mislabels the mechanism. The phrase is only defensible as a description of the code's stated *intent* (Telemetry.luau:8 "funnelSessionId nil: documented-optional, fine for one-time funnels"), not of its behaviour.

claims.finding:
The upper bound holds; the lower bound does not hold "everywhere", and the upper bound is about the ROOM, not the SERVER.

WHAT IS TRUE (upper bound, room membership). In MainGame there is exactly ONE write that can grow room.members: RoomService:172 `table.insert(room.members, {`, guarded one line above by `if #room.members >= Config.Room.MaxPlayers then return end` (:171). The only two other paths that add anyone re-check the same cap before calling it (promoteSpectators :189, seat :401). I confirmed this against the LIVE place, not just the mirror: a weppy search of all 34 scripts under game.ServerScriptService for `room.members,` returns exactly three RoomService hits (insert :172, snapshot :300, remove :322) plus three read-only uses in MachineFlow/Minefield/CanteenProtocol, and a search for `MaxPlayers` returns 5 hits, all in RoomService. No 5th player can become a member. dev-src is equally tight: addMember has three call sites (409 fresh room, 454, 577) and the latter two are gated by roomCanAccept with no yield between check and insert.

WHAT IS FALSE (lower bound). "No path lets a match run with 1" is false as written. Two independent paths break it.

(1) STUDIO, MainGame, and it is in the LIVE place. RoomService:93-98 `local function minPlayers() if RunService:IsStudio() then return Config.Players.StudioTestMinimum end return Config.Room.MinPlayers end`, and GameConfig:17 `StudioTestMinimum = 1`. I read BOTH of these out of the live datamodel via weppy get_source, so this is not a mirror-staleness artifact. Every gate that defends the floor (maybeAutoStart :314, RoomStartRequest :622, the post-countdown recheck :290) calls minPlayers(), so in Studio they all pass at 1. Worse, the snapshot at :300 is `room.requiredMinimum = math.min(#room.members, minPlayers())` = min(1,1) = 1, so the mid-match abort at :335 never fires either — the solo match runs to completion. This is deliberate and documented ("Studio solo/debug path only; never used on a live server"), and the rest of the codebase is built for it: Pacing.luau:26-31 clamps `n <= 2` onto the 2-player row with the comment "Solo is deliberately mapped onto the 2-player row", and tests/rules.lua:74 asserts it. The cost is that the 2-player floor is the one rule that is never exercised in the environment where the game is actually tested. dev-src's own GameConfig:6-9 names this exact defect and says it was removed there — studio-src still ships it.

(2) dev-src (Kenopsia_DEV), remote-reachable, no minimum check at all. RoomService.forceStart:316-318 calls beginCountdown directly, and beginCountdown:270-299 contains no player-count test of any kind — unlike its studio-src counterpart, which rechecks at :290. Its only caller is PlaylistService:209-220, the OnServerEvent handler for a RemoteEvent named "TrialPracticeRequest" that is created unconditionally at boot (Main.server.luau:10 `PlaylistService.start(RoomService)`). The handler's entire guard is: caller has a room, room.phase == "Waiting", and caller is the host. A player alone in a party they just created satisfies all three — createRoom:399 sets hostUserId to the creator and addMember:409 makes them the sole member. The run then proceeds through the full 3-trial playlist, because the liveness predicate is `#room.members > 0` (PlaylistService:45). Note that the LEGITIMATE path is guarded — setReady:598 refuses a ready flag below minPlayers() — so forceStart is a bypass of the only floor the DEV place has. And no client in the repo fires TrialPracticeRequest (a grep of all of dev-src finds the string only inside PlaylistService), which means there is no UI for it and any client that fires it is by definition an exploit client.

WHAT IS UNPROVEN (the 5th player, at server scope). The claim conflates room capacity with server capacity. Nothing in the shipped server code reads Players.MaxPlayers — I searched all 34 live ServerScriptService scripts and got zero hits outside RoomService's own Config.Room.MaxPlayers. The legacy code DID guard this (docs/legacy/src/server/init.server.luau:24-27 warns when Players.MaxPlayers exceeds Config.MaxPlayers); the current code dropped it. Published server size is a Creator Dashboard setting, readable from neither source nor the edit-mode API — my weppy `get game.Players` returned an empty property list, and the repo's own docs (docs/place/07-FINDINGS.md:82-85) state flatly that it is readable through no API and no MCP call. The repo asserts MainGame = 4, but PHASE1-CORRECTIONS.md:12-13 says that was "Accepted on the reviewer's attestation", i.e. it is an unverified claim, and 07-FINDINGS.md:80 says Kenopsia_DEV is separately at 28. Meanwhile the codebase carries a complete bench/spectator subsystem whose purpose is players beyond the seated four (RoomService.spectators; MachineFlow:1461-1474 firing "YOU ARE ON THE BENCH. / THE NEXT CYCLE TAKES YOU."; the live client's bench state at KenopsiaClient:542 `local maxPlayers = 4` and :2541-2560). So players 5..N are ADMITTED TO THE SERVER wherever capacity allows — they simply never become members.

Two supporting defects found on the way. GameConfig.Players.MaximumPerServer and .MinimumForMatch are read by NO code in either tree — a grep over studio-src and dev-src returns only the definitions. They are decorative, which means GameConfig:11-13's instruction that "Published capacity must match this" is enforced by nothing, and it is why dev-src can carry `MaximumPerServer = 8` while its own Room.MaxPlayers is 4 and its documented server size is 28, a three-way disagreement that costs nothing because nobody reads it. Separately, MachineFlow:1366 hardcodes `openSeats = 4 - #room.members` instead of Config.Room.MaxPlayers (confirmed live at the same line) — a second copy of the cap that will not follow a config change.

claims.fixSketch: Three separable changes, in order of value. First, delete Config.Players.StudioTestMinimum and collapse studio-src RoomService's minPlayers() to `return Config.Room.MinPlayers`, exactly as dev-src already did and documented in its own GameConfig header — testing solo then requires two Studio clients, which is what "Start Server + 2 Players" is for, and the floor becomes a rule that testing actually exercises. Second, in dev-src either delete forceStart and the TrialPracticeRequest handler outright (nothing in the repo calls the remote, so it is pure attack surface) or, if the practice run is wanted, move the `#room.members >= minPlayers()` test inside beginCountdown so no caller can route around it — the test belongs at the gate, not at each caller, which is the structural reason studio-src's version survives and dev-src's does not. Third, make the capacity constants load-bearing instead of decorative: have the server boot read Players.MaxPlayers and warn (or refuse) when it exceeds Config.Players.MaximumPerServer, restoring what docs/legacy/src/server/init.server.luau:24-27 used to do, and replace MachineFlow:1366's literal 4 with Config.Room.MaxPlayers so one number governs the cap. That converts an unverifiable Dashboard attestation into a boot-time assertion that shows up in the log of every live server.

claims.finding:
TRUE: "nothing to do" and "no practice". FALSE: "may be bounced straight back / menu<->game ping-pong" — both ends of that loop are explicitly closed, and the actual failure is the opposite one (stranding).

(1) NOTHING TO DO — CONFIRMED. The MainGame waiting room is a bare 44x44 box built in code: floor, four walls, ceiling, one lamp panel, one SpawnLocation, and nothing else [SOURCE Lobby.luau:69-87]. Zero occurrences of practice/tutorial/training anywhere in studio-src [SOURCE grep]. The live StarterGui contains exactly 19 GuiButtons; the only ones a waiting player can touch are Btn_READY, Btn_SETTINGS + five settings rows + CLOSE, plus KenopsiaEmote.DanceButton and FieldPushGui.HeadbuttButton (the rest are TouchControls for in-trial input) [RUNTIME live-gui.md:218-241]. Pressing READY alone is ACCEPTED by the server — live RoomService's setReady has no minimum-players gate (minPlayers() is called only at lines 93/290/300/314/335/622, none of them in setReady) — and then silently does nothing, because maybeAutoStart returns early below 2 members [SOURCE studio-src RoomService:314; LIVE weppy search confirms identical line numbers]. There is no feedback: the LIVE client contains ZERO occurrences of "WAITING" [RUNTIME weppy search on game.StarterPlayer.StarterPlayerScripts.KenopsiaClient → matchesFound 0], and no "MINIMUM n PLAYERS" string (that text exists only in the MENU client, dev-src PartyWallView:936). No invite affordance either: SocialClient fires PromptGameInvite only on a "shiftreport" packet, which a player who never completes a round never receives [SOURCE SocialClient:78-84]; its own header says a lobby invite button "belongs to the UI", and no such button exists (zero "invite" matches in studio-src outside SocialClient, zero in the live client). The sole content a lone arrival gets is the 6.4 s trial roulette plus a static info panel, shown once — preFlow does run for a single member (#room.members > 0), and the preShown latch keeps it from ever running again [SOURCE/RUNTIME MachineFlow:1498-1500, live line numbers identical].

(2) NO PRACTICE — CONFIRMED, and worse than claimed. MainGame has no practice at all. The MENU place does have one server-side: a host-only TrialPracticeRequest that runs the three sharpening trials locally without teleporting [SOURCE dev-src PlaylistService:207-220]. But NO client anywhere fires that remote — a repo-wide grep finds "TrialPracticeRequest" in exactly two files, dev-src/PlaylistService.luau:208 and the weppy snapshot of that same module. Practice ships dark: no button, no keybind.

(3) BOUNCED STRAIGHT BACK / PING-PONG — REFUTED, on both legs.
  (a) MainGame side: SoloExit.shouldSend is `hadCompanyFlag == true and remainingCount == 1`; hadCompany starts false and only flips true once the server has actually seen two players [RUNTIME live get_source SoloExit:56-72, 112-140 — byte-identical to the mirror]. A player who ARRIVES alone is therefore never sent back. The module header names the claimed failure mode verbatim as the reason the gate exists: "eine Endlosschleife zwischen zwei Places, in der das Spiel nie startet" [SOURCE SoloExit:30-35].
  (b) Menu side: the menu never dispatches a solo player in the first place. The only menu→MainGame teleport (PlaylistService:169) is reachable only from RunRequested with practiceRun unset, which only fires from beginCountdown, which is gated on minPlayers()=2 in maybeAutoStart (dev RoomService:311), in startRun (:625-628), and even in setReady (:598-601 refuses READY below 2). forceStart is the practice path and sets practiceRun, so RunRequested runs the playlist locally instead of teleporting [SOURCE PlaylistService:222-231]. The countdown aborts if anyone leaves [dev RoomService:336-338]. dev minPlayers() has no Studio bypass, deliberately [dev RoomService:65-67; dev GameConfig:6-9]. So the return leg cannot restart the loop either.

WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENS INSTEAD — the inverse bug. A player who does end up alone in a fresh MainGame server (party-mate's teleport failed, or dropped in the window between PlaylistService:169 firing and arrival — teleportRoom skips absent members at :149-152) is STRANDED, not bounced. hadCompany is false so SoloExit never fires; the LIVE client contains zero Teleport calls [RUNTIME weppy search "Teleport" → matchesFound 0]; there is no return-to-menu button among the 19 [RUNTIME live-gui.md:216-243]; and the one string that looks like an exit, "BACK TO MENU" on the podium end card, is only an un-ready and appears only after a completed session [RUNTIME live client 3997, 4061-4063]. The exit the claim says fires too eagerly is in fact the one thing that would rescue this player, and it is gated off.

RESIDUAL HAZARD (real, but not the claim). hadCompany is never reset to false. On a MainGame server that accepts public joins and outlives its last pair, a fresh solo joiner inherits hadCompany=true and the 5 s watch teleports them out — after the module-wide 10 s RETRY_SECONDS lock, which is shared across ALL players (SoloExit:92-94), so one player's attempt also blocks another's. That is a one-way bounce with no return leg, not a ping-pong. Whether MainGame accepts public joins at all is NEEDS_RUNTIME; the menu path uses ReserveServer (PlaylistService:166-169), so party-created servers are private and cannot receive a stray solo joiner.

maps.summary: The menu place is a self-contained, in-memory party lobby with no persistence and no cross-place messaging. RoomService owns parties for the lifetime of one menu server; PartyRegistry (the MemoryStore code) is present in the place tree but is never required by anything and is completely dead. The only exit to MainGame is PlaylistService.teleportRoom: RoomService fires RunRequested after a 5-second countdown, PlaylistService reserves a server on 110672791536316 and calls TeleportAsync with the whole live roster. TeleportData is never set — the TeleportOptions object carries only ReservedServerAccessCode, so MainGame receives no roster, no room id, no host and no trial selection; membership is implied purely by who arrives. A lone player cannot press play: three independent server gates and the wall UI all enforce Config.Room.MinPlayers = 2, and the shipped dev client never fires RoomStartRequest, RoomQuickJoinRequest or TrialPracticeRequest at all (there are exactly two FireServer call sites in the entire dev client). The menu place touches no DataStore whatsoever — MainGame's KenopsiaProfile_v1 / key "u_%d" is written only in studio-src, so nothing a player does in the menu survives the session. There is no handshake in either direction: no MessagingService in dev-src, no GetJoinData anywhere, and SoloExit sends a lone MainGame survivor back with a bare TeleportAsync(MENU_PLACE_ID, {plr}) carrying no options and no data. A returning player is therefore indistinguishable from a fresh joiner and sees the ordinary landing screen with no explanation. Ping-pong is impossible from the menu side: the return leg is automatic but the outbound leg requires two players who have both pressed READY, and the READY row is disabled below two.

nodes.role: Boot. Starts exactly three services in order: RoomService, PlaylistService(RoomService), MenuPresenceService(RoomService). Notably does NOT require PartyRegistry.

The whole party authority. Rooms live in three plain tables (rooms/byCode/byPlayer) for the lifetime of this one server. Creates all 15 lobby RemoteEvents, validates every inbound payload, owns phase Waiting/Starting/Playing, the 5s countdown, host migration, join-approval queue, and the RunRequested BindableEvent that is the single handover to PlaylistService.

Two jobs behind one signal. On RunRequested it either runs a LOCAL 3-trial practice playlist inside the menu server (when room.practiceRun is set) or teleports the whole room to MainGame. Holds MAIN_PLACE_ID and the only ReserveServer/TeleportAsync in dev-src.

Owns the player's character while the menu is up: parks it on MenuStage.CharacterAnchor, zeroes WalkSpeed/JumpPower, anchors the root, drops collisions, hides the nametag. Sole writer of the player attribute KenopsiaMenuActive. Releases on RunRequested plus a 1 Hz reconcile loop.

DEAD CODE. A MemoryStore hash-map cross-server code registry (claim/lookup/release/touch). Present in the place tree via kenopsia-dev.project.json:29 but required by nothing, so its GetHashMap call at module scope never even executes.

Shared numbers: Room.MaxPlayers 4, Room.MinPlayers 2, CodeLength 6, BrowseLimit 15, MaxPendingJoinRequests 8, JoinRequestLifetimeSeconds 45, RoomTtlSeconds 3600, MemoryStore.RoomMapName. Read by RoomService, PlaylistService, PartyRegistry and SessionWallController.
Practice-only trial (Setup/Start/Stop/Cleanup/HandleInput). Runs only inside the menu server's practice playlist; unrelated to MainGame's CANTEEN PROTOCOL.
Practice-only trial, same contract.
Practice-only trial, same contract.

Client boot. Waits up to 20s for PlayerGui.KenopsiaGui (a live-only object, not in the Rojo tree), then constructs MenuController, MenuSceneController, MenuOverlayController, SessionWallController, TrialController, each under its own xpcall so one failure does not take the menu down.
Owns the CRT monitor surface used by trial screens and the settings appliers. Subscribes to RoomState for the trial path only (Countdown / Playing / Waiting). Never fires a remote.
The flat landing layer: START / SETTINGS / CREDITS. START is purely a camera move to the session wall — it sends nothing to the server. This is what a returning player sees.
3D street camera and head-look. Engages/releases purely off the KenopsiaMenuActive attribute; it decides nothing itself.
The only network client for the lobby. Builds a SurfaceGui adorned to MenuStage.SessionDisplay and fires exactly 8 of the 15 lobby remotes. Holds the single FireServer call site for the party path.
Renders the wall terminal (Select/Create/Join/Browse/Waiting/Room pages, 4 member slots, approval modal). Disables the READY row below minPlayers — the client-side half of the lone-player block.
Practice-playlist screens. Holds the only other FireServer in the dev client (TrialInput).
Palette/fonts/party metrics. Line 120 is the explicit statement that the menu has no DataStore by design.
Menu SFX + music gate.
Tween helpers used by the screens.
Custom pointer; owns MouseIconEnabled.
Animated wordmark on the landing.
Standard character Animate script for the menu rig. No menu or party coupling.

S->C room snapshot (roomId, code, isPublic, joinPolicy, hostUserId, phase, countdown, memberCount, maxPlayers, minPlayers, members[]). Two listeners: SessionWallController (party) and MenuController (trial screens).
S->C sanitized public-room list, capped at BrowseLimit.
S->C Pending/Accepted/Declined/Expired/Cancelled for the requester.
S->host-only approval queue; survives host migration.
S->C error string. Created by RoomService, also fired by PlaylistService for teleport failures.
C->S {public:boolean, joinPolicy:'Open'|'Approval'}, exact-key validated, 2/s.
C->S 6-char code join, 2/s.
C->S refresh browse list, 2/s.
C->S join a public room by roomId, 2/s.
C->S host accept/decline, 5/s.
C->S withdraw a pending request, 2/s.
C->S leave party, 3/s.
C->S boolean ready, 5/s. THE ONLY path the shipped client has to a run.
C->S host force-start. Server handler exists (startRun) but NO client in dev-src ever fires it — orphaned surface.
C->S legacy auto-join-best-public. Server handler exists, no client caller in dev-src — orphaned surface.
C->S host-only practice run. Created by PlaylistService, no client caller in dev-src. It is the ONLY route to forceStart, which is the only start path with no player-count check.
S->C practice-trial packets: kind = intro | begin | trialResult | finalResult plus per-trial kinds, all carrying a run token.
C->S practice-trial input, 25/s, token-matched against the live run.
Player attribute. Server-authoritative single source of truth for 'this player is standing in the menu'. Written only by MenuPresenceService, read only by MenuSceneController.

LIVE-ONLY ScreenGui (Monitor.ScreenArea.Content.Screens + Overlay + Backdrop). Not in kenopsia-dev.project.json, so it exists only in the published place. Ships Enabled=false; MenuController raises it only for trial screens.
SurfaceGui built at runtime and adorned to workspace.MenuStage.SessionDisplay. The whole party UI lives here.
LIVE-ONLY BasePart in workspace.MenuStage. Where every menu character is parked and anchored. Absent from the Rojo tree.
LIVE-ONLY BasePart the party wall is adorned to. Polled for 10s; if absent the wall never renders.
placeId 110672791536316. Teleport destination, always a freshly reserved (private) server.
placeId 129909297895850. This place. Also SoloExit's return destination — reached with a bare TeleportAsync, i.e. a PUBLIC matchmade menu server.
MainGame side of the return path. shouldSend(remaining, hadCompany) = hadCompany and remaining == 1. Fires on PlayerRemoving and on a 5s watch, 10s retry floor, suppressed during BindToClose.
The ONLY DataStore user in either place. Store KenopsiaProfile_v1, key format u_%d, UpdateAsync-only with a {jobId, ts} session lock and a BindToClose flush.
The ONLY MessagingService user in either place. Publishes and subscribes topic KenopsiaGrant_v1 and documents a DEV->MainGame publisher that does not exist.
Standard DataStore, keys u_<userId>. Written and read ONLY from MainGame. The menu place never opens it.
MemoryStore hash map name declared for PartyRegistry. Never actually touched at runtime because PartyRegistry is never required.
MessagingService topic, payload {kind='emote', userId, id}. Subscribed in MainGame. dev-src contains no MessagingService call of any kind, so the documented DEV publisher does not exist.

risks: PING-PONG: NOT POSSIBLE from the menu side, and here is the code that decides it. Three independent server gates all read Config.Room.MinPlayers = 2 (GameConfig.luau:19): RoomService.luau:311 `if Config.Room.RequireAllReady and room.phase == "Waiting" and #room.members >= minPlayers() and allReady(room) then` (the auto-start), RoomService.luau:598-599 `if ready and #room.members < minPlayers() then fail(player, string.format("MINIMUM %d PLAYERS", minPlayers()))` (a lone player cannot even mark himself ready), and RoomService.luau:625-627 `if #room.members < minPlayers() then fail(player, "NOT ENOUGH PLAYERS")` (force-start). The UI blocks it a fourth time at PartyWallView.luau:943 `local canReady = count >= minPlayers and room.phase ~= "Playing"`. The one start path with NO count check is RoomService.luau:316-318 forceStart, but its only caller sets room.practiceRun first (PlaylistService.luau:218) and PlaylistService.luau:225-227 routes that to the LOCAL playlist, never to teleportRoom. So a lone returning player physically cannot re-teleport himself to MainGame, automatically or manually.

The return leg is automatic while the outbound leg is manual and needs a second human. A player SoloExit'd back arrives in a PUBLIC menu server (SoloExit.luau:104 passes no TeleportOptions) with an empty party and must find a stranger or a friend to play again. That is the intended design, but it means the menu place is where a solo player permanently comes to rest.

A lone arrival in MainGame is a dead end with no exit. SoloExit.luau:70 `return hadCompanyFlag == true and remainingCount == 1` — hadCompany only becomes true once the server has actually held two players (SoloExit.luau:116-118, :135-138). A reserved MainGame server that only ever receives one player never sets it, so that player is never sent back. Reachable via the teleportRoom race (PlaylistService.luau:154, no >=2 check) or if the second player's teleport fails during loading.

Every lobby remote is reachable by any client, and three of them have no legitimate caller. An exploiter in the menu place can fire TrialPracticeRequest (PlaylistService.luau:209) and, as host of a one-man room, reach forceStart -> beginCountdown with no member-count check at all — running the practice playlist solo. Rate limits are per-second only (PlaylistService.luau:210 `allow(player, 2)`), not per-session.

Party codes are per-server only. RoomService.luau:19 `local byCode = {}` is a plain table in one server's memory, and PartyRegistry (the cross-server registry) is dormant. Two friends who join the menu place at the same time land in different public menu servers roughly as often as not, and the code one gives the other will return 'UNKNOWN CODE' (RoomService.luau:418) with no hint that the reason is server sharding.

The menu place persists nothing. Theme.luau:120 `-- Session settings. No DataStore in the MVP by design, so these reset on leave.` Text scale, retro filter, scanlines, reduce-effects, reduce-flicker, animations, cursor, UI sound and music (MenuController.luau:64-74) are all rebuilt at defaults every join — including every SoloExit return. A player bounced back from MainGame loses every accessibility setting they had chosen.
