maps.area: persistence (Profiles / Badges / ProgressionRules / DataStore + MemoryStore use across both places)
maps.summary: All progression persistence in Kenopsia lives in exactly one module: studio-src/ServerScriptService/KenopsiaServer/Services/Profiles.luau, which owns the single DataStore "KenopsiaProfile_v1" keyed "u_%d" (userId). [RUNTIME] I confirmed against the connected live MainGame Studio (placeId 110672791536316): across all 115 scripts in the place, GetDataStore appears only in Profiles (lines 621, 625), and the two UpdateAsync call sites are Profiles:110 (load) and Profiles:132 (save) — there is no SetAsync anywhere. The design is volatile-first: every joiner immediately gets an in-memory ProgressionRules.defaultProfile() and play only ever touches that table; the DataStore is best-effort background traffic. The session lock is `_lock = { jobId = game.JobId, ts = os.time() }` — jobId plus timestamp, with NO per-load nonce/GUID — stealable after 180 s. The critical structural gap: trySave never inspects the stored `_lock` before overwriting, and there is no per-player queue, mutex or in-flight flag, so several code paths can have two UpdateAsync calls in flight on the same key at once. Writes happen at four places (loader "left while loading" branch, PlayerRemoving, the fire-and-forget flush thread, BindToClose); flush is called from the verdict loop (MachineFlow:1325) and from two EmoteService grant paths. A slow load is destructive: when the stored profile lands it replaces the live table wholesale (`entry.data = data`, Profiles:244), so anything earned during the load window is discarded. A "cannot save" state is computed and put on the wire (the `volatile` field in the profilestate and shiftreport packets) but [RUNTIME] nothing in the live place renders it: 0 matches for "profilestate" across the 28 StarterPlayer scripts, 0 matches for "OFFLINE" across all 115 scripts, and the sole shiftreport consumer (SocialClient:78) reads only openSeats. The DEV/menu place (129909297895850, dev-src/) has zero DataStore code — it only uses a MemoryStore HashMap "KenopsiaRooms_v1" for 6-char party codes — so no progression is read or written there at all.

nodes.role: The ONLY DataStore owner in the game. Volatile-first in-memory profile per userId in `live`; session lock, migrate, merge-write, three flush moments, BindToClose. 663 lines; [RUNTIME] live copy is also 663 lines and byte-identical in the lock/save/flush regions I sampled.
The one persistent store. Key format "u_%d" (Profiles:40) => key `u_<UserId>`. Value = the profile table plus a non-owned `_lock` field.

[RUNTIME] the ONLY consumer of the shiftreport packet anywhere in the live place; reads packet.openSeats only, ignores xp/clearance/volatile.
Boot order. Profiles.start() runs before EmoteService.start() and MachineFlow.start(), so the profile tables exist before any verdict or emote read.
Fires RunRequested exactly once per match (phase+token gate), which is what keeps the verdict — and therefore recordSession — from running twice per session.
Teleports the last remaining player to the DEV/menu place. This is the event that empties a MainGame server and therefore races the final save.
AnalyticsService funnel only — NOT persistence. Profiles calls Telemetry.funnel(plr, "KenopsiaRetention", 1, "Joined") after a successful load.
The DEV place's only store use: a MemoryStore HashMap, not a DataStore. Party-code claim/lookup/release/touch.
MemoryStore HashMap (NOT a DataStore). Key = a 6-char code from alphabet "ABCDEFGHJKLMNPQRSTUVWXYZ23456789"; TTL 3600 s. Holds {accessCode, privateServerId, placeId, createdAt}.
ReserveServer + TeleportAsync into MainGame 110672791536316. The entry edge into the only place that persists anything.
Requires ONLY RoomService, PlaylistService, MenuPresenceService — no Profiles, no DataStore. The menu place persists nothing.
MessagingService topic for cross-place emote grants. MainGame subscribes (EmoteService:479); NOTHING in dev-src publishes to it.

risks: LOCK RE-STAMP AFTER RELEASE -> the player is locked out of their own profile for up to 180 s. Profiles.luau:140 `stored._lock = { jobId = game.JobId, ts = os.time() }` runs on every non-release save. If a flush write (release=false, Profiles.luau:473) lands AFTER onLeave's release write (release=true, :279), the stored profile is left locked by a server the player has already left, with a brand-new timestamp. tryLoad on any other server then hits :112 `if lockHeldByOther(stored, now) then blocked = true` and returns 'locked by another server' (:124) for all 3 attempts (LOAD_ATTEMPTS = 3, :42) — the player falls through to permanently VOLATILE for that server, and because flush (:470) and onLeave (:277) both early-return on entry.volatile, NOTHING that session is ever written. NEEDS_RUNTIME to prove the ordering actually inverts; see uncertainties.

STALE WRITE ONTO A NEWER SESSION -> silent rollback. Because trySave (Profiles.luau:132-143) never checks who holds `_lock`, a late-landing write from server A overwrites every OWNED_FIELD (:92-96: xp, clearance, sessions, streak, quests, emotes, crates, trialStats, ...) on a key that server B has already loaded. If B loaded BEFORE A's write landed, B's in-memory copy is now ahead of a store that just went backwards, and B's own next save will write B's copy — which was built from the pre-A snapshot. Net effect: session A's progress disappears. There is no version counter, no CAS, and no `_lock` comparison to detect it.

CONCURRENT SAME-KEY WRITES ARE REACHABLE FROM A CLIENT-ADJACENT PATH. EmoteService.luau:459-468 (PromptGamePassPurchaseFinished) and :479-483 (MessagingService subscriber) both end in `pcall(Profiles.flush, userId)` (:278 / :260) with no coordination against MachineFlow.luau:1325's verdict flush. Because the dirty flag is only cleared post-write (Profiles.luau:145), both flushes pass the gate and both spawn a trySave. The payload is the same table reference so the DATA is identical; the divergence is in `_lock` and in DataStore write-throttle pressure on one key.

LOAD-WINDOW PROGRESS IS DOUBLE-LOST. During the up-to-~7 s load window (LOAD_ATTEMPTS 3 x LOAD_BACKOFF {2,5}, Profiles.luau:42-43) the entry is volatile, so (a) no write can happen at all — flush returns false at :470 and onLeave returns at :277 — and (b) when the stored profile finally lands it is `entry.data = data` (:244), discarding whatever was recorded meanwhile. A player who joins mid-session and reaches a verdict inside that window earns nothing and is told nothing.

BINDTOCLOSE CAN CUT OFF THE LAST PLAYER'S FINAL SAVE. onLeave removes the entry from `live` before saving (Profiles.luau:276 then :279), and BindToClose only waits on `live` (:644-645, :655). SoloExit teleports the last remaining player out (SoloExit.luau:104), which is precisely when the server begins shutting down — so the very save that matters most (release + lastSeen for the last player) is the one nobody waits for. CLOSE_FLUSH_SECONDS = 25 (:44) protects only entries still in `live`.

NO SESSION-LEVEL IDEMPOTENCY ON THE XP/COUNTER HALF OF THE VERDICT. recordSession increments sessions, viableCount/rejectedCount and xp unconditionally (Profiles.luau:323, 326/328, 399). The quest payout and the streak tick ARE idempotent (ProgressionRules.luau:301-307; :131-133), so a duplicate verdict would pay no quest XP but WOULD double the session XP and inflate the lifetime counters. Nothing in the profile records which sessionId has been consumed. Today the only thing preventing a double verdict is RoomService's phase/token gate (RoomService.luau:277, 284, 289) — a single-point protection outside the persistence layer.

SILENT FAILURE BY DESIGN, WITH NO OPERATOR SIGNAL AFTER THE FIRST EVENT. warnOnce (Profiles.luau:58-62) latches per key for the server's lifetime, so a server where every load fails prints ONE line ('load failed (expected in Studio without API access)', :249) and then nothing. There is no counter, no Telemetry event on load/save failure (Telemetry is only called on SUCCESS, :261), and no AnalyticsService signal. A production server silently running fully volatile would look identical to a healthy one from outside.

MIGRATION IS ONE-WAY AND UNGUARDED AGAINST TYPE CORRUPTION AT THE TOP LEVEL. migrate/fillMissing (Profiles.luau:72-88) only fills MISSING keys; a stored value of the wrong TYPE (e.g. a string where a number belongs) passes straight through. Individual consumers hand-guard the ones that would throw — crates at :380-390, streak via tickStreak, emotes via emoteState (:504-514), quests via applyQuests — but xp, sessions, roundsPlayed, viableCount, rejectedCount, bestBand and clearance are only tonumber'd at point of use, and `data.analytics.d1Stamp` at :341 is dereferenced with no type guard at all (a non-table `analytics` would throw inside recordSession, which the header at :300 promises never happens).
uncertainties: Whether Roblox actually delivers two concurrent same-key UpdateAsync requests from one server in issue order. Every 'late-landing write' risk above depends on it. NEEDS_RUNTIME. The observation that settles it: a play test on the live MainGame server where one player triggers an emote grant (EmoteService.luau:260 flush) and disconnects within the same second, followed by reading key `u_<UserId>` from KenopsiaProfile_v1 and inspecting `_lock`. If `_lock` is non-nil after the player is gone, the flush write landed after the release write and the lockout scenario is real. I could not run this — it requires DataStore access and a running server, both of which are outside a read-only pass.

Whether the lockout actually reproduces end to end. NEEDS_RUNTIME: two MainGame servers, player leaves A immediately after a verdict and joins B within 180 s, then read B's server log for the warnOnce string 'load failed (expected in Studio without API access): locked by another server' (Profiles.luau:249 formatting :124's message) and check whether Profiles.isVolatile returns true for them on B.

Whether the load-window overwrite is reachable in real play. It needs a recordTrial/recordSession/grantEmote to land inside the up-to-~7 s window at Profiles.luau:229-254. NEEDS_RUNTIME: instrument nothing, just observe — join a MainGame server with API access throttled, and check whether a player who joins mid-trial has a trialStats row for that trial after their next verdict.

maps.area: MainGame (placeId 110672791536316) — arrival and lobby: Main.server.luau boot, Lobby, RoomService (canonical room lifecycle / READY consent / abort), SoloExit, CharacterService, GameConfig, Pacing.
maps.summary: MainGame boots one Script (ServerScriptService.KenopsiaServer.Main) that requires 8 modules and then calls 8 .start() functions in a fixed order: Lobby, SoloExit, RoomService, Telemetry, Profiles, EmoteService, CharacterService, MachineFlow [SOURCE Main.server.luau:5-21; RUNTIME live source identical, 24 lines]. Lobby.ensure() builds workspace.KenopsiaLobby and, critically, workspace.SpawnLocation at runtime — neither exists in the saved place [RUNTIME find_child SpawnLocation under game.Workspace = found:false]. RoomService owns exactly one room (id 1) that is never destroyed, only reset; its phase takes five values (Waiting, Starting, Playing, Aborting, Cleanup) and its sub-stage six (nil, Selecting, Briefing, Trial, Score, FinalScore). RoomService creates the 8 Room* remotes at start; ReplicatedStorage.Kenopsia.Remotes likewise does not exist in the saved place [RUNTIME: "Instance not found: game.ReplicatedStorage.Kenopsia.Remotes"]. Seating is NOT driven by Players.PlayerAdded — RoomService connects PlayerAdded nowhere [RUNTIME script search "PlayerAdded" in live RoomService: 0 matches]; the only seating path in shipped code is MachineFlow's 2-second watchdog, which stamps KenopsiaJoinedAt, waits >7 s, then calls RoomService.autoSeat. READY is collected server-authoritatively on RoomReadyRequest and the full who-is-ready set is broadcast to every player on the server inside the RoomState packet's `members` array. A match starts only through maybeAutoStart (RequireAllReady + minPlayers + allReady) → beginCountdown → 3-second countdown → phase Playing → RunRequested:Fire(room.id); the manual RoomStartRequest path exists but no shipped client fires it. Abort is a three-part mechanism: abortCountdown (Starting→Waiting, 3 reason strings), abortMatch (Playing→Aborting, 3 reason strings, double-guarded), and cleanupToWaiting (any non-Waiting phase → Cleanup → Waiting, 4 reason strings from MachineFlow). SoloExit is the only TeleportService call in the whole MainGame tree: it sends the last remaining player to place 129909297895850 the moment headcount drops to 1, provided the server has ever held 2+ players.

BindableEvent. The one server-internal signal that a match has begun. Fires the room ID (a number), never the table, because BindableEvents deep-copy tables.

risks: [RUNTIME] SERVER CAPACITY IS 60, NOT 4. The live MainGame Edit datamodel reports Players.MaxPlayers = 60 (weppy manage_properties get on game.Players, placeId 110672791536316), while GameConfig.luau:11-14 states `Published capacity must match this ... MaximumPerServer = 4` and the room seats 4. With a 60-cap server, players 5..60 are permanently spectators: seat() sends them to addSpectator (RoomService.luau:401-405) and promoteSpectators only takes them while #members < 4 (:189). It also disarms SoloExit entirely, because headcount never reaches 1. NEEDS_RUNTIME to settle whether the PUBLISHED server size differs from the Edit-datamodel value: read Players.MaxPlayers from a running live server (or open File > Game Settings > Places > Server Size). This is the single highest-impact finding in the area.

[SOURCE] SEATING HAS A SINGLE POINT OF FAILURE AND A KILL SWITCH. RoomService connects Players.PlayerAdded nowhere ([RUNTIME] script search of the live RoomService for 'PlayerAdded': 0 matches), so the ONLY way anyone is ever seated is MachineFlow.luau:1456 `RoomServiceRef.autoSeat(plr)` inside a loop wrapped in `if not workspace:GetAttribute("KenopsiaNoAuto") then` (:1447). Setting that one workspace attribute, or any error that prevents MachineFlow.start from reaching line 1444, means nobody is ever seated, no READY is ever accepted (setReady rejects non-members with 'SPECTATING - NEXT MATCH', :352-355) and no match can ever start. [RUNTIME] the attribute is currently unset (game.Workspace attributeCount 0), so the path is live today.

[SOURCE] SoloExit's `hadCompany` latches TRUE FOR THE LIFE OF THE SERVER and is never reset (set at SoloExit.luau:117, :135, :137; no assignment to false anywhere in the file). Consequence: once two players have been on a server, any later solo occupant is teleported out. Concretely — a 2-player party finishes, both leave, the server lingers, one new player joins alone: headcount 1 and hadCompany still true, so the 5-second watch (:151-156) bounces them within 5 s. The module's own docstring (:27-35) argues hadCompany distinguishes 'allein UEBRIG' from 'allein ANGEKOMMEN', but a latched flag cannot make that distinction after the original company has gone. NEEDS_RUNTIME: join a live MainGame server that previously held 2+ players, alone, and observe whether the '[SoloExit] armed'/teleport path fires.

[SOURCE] SoloExit fires BEFORE RoomService learns the player left. Main.server.luau:15 runs SoloExit.start() and :16 runs RoomService.start(), so SoloExit's Players.PlayerRemoving handler (SoloExit.luau:140) is connected first and Roblox invokes connections in registration order. On a 2-player match where one quits, the survivor's TeleportAsync is issued before removeMember reaches abortMatch("PLAYER LEFT - CANNOT CONTINUE WITH A SINGLE PLAYER") (RoomService.luau:340). The AbortScreen card (AbortScreen.client.luau:93) may therefore be raced by the teleport and never read. NEEDS_RUNTIME: a 2-player live test where one player quits mid-trial, watching whether the survivor sees the abort card before the loading screen.

maps.area: Session spine — studio-src/ServerScriptService/KenopsiaServer/Services/MachineFlow.luau (1514 lines), read in full, plus RoomService.luau, Contexts.luau, Pacing.luau, AudienceCam.luau, Podium.luau, TrialKit.luau and the (STALE) KenopsiaClient.client.luau mirror.
maps.summary: MachineFlow owns everything inside RoomService's Playing phase and drives one linear beat chain: lobby preFlow (roulette -> info card) -> runMatch -> per trial (Selecting -> Briefing -> Trial) -> per round (round card -> optional role card -> hide -> cover -> respawn grace -> guarded round -> cover -> standings -> settle) -> trial score board -> FinalScore verdict -> ShiftReport -> a single finalizer. There are 11 distinct hold() call sites, 17 early-return points inside the xpcall body plus 2 in preFlow, and 10 distinct packet kinds leaving this file (selection, info, status, round, rolecard, hide, cover, score, shiftreport, audiencecam). runRoundGuarded returns (ok, result) on a completed round, (false, "timeout") when its RoundSeconds+35s budget expires, and (false, "aborted") when it observes room.aborting; both call sites treat anything that is not exactly "timeout" as a fatal error and re-raise it, so the ONLY producer of "aborted" (a player leaving mid-round, via RoomService.removeMember -> abortMatch) drives outcome = "error" and reaches the RoomServiceRef.abort(room, "MINIGAME ERROR") call at line 1398 — but that call is a guaranteed no-op, because abortMatch's first guard rejects any phase that is not Playing/Starting and the room is already "Aborting". So a player-cancellation reaches the MINIGAME ERROR call site but never its effect; the players see the earlier "RUN ABORTED - PLAYER LEFT..." card instead, while the server log mislabels the session as "failed: aborted" and cleans up with reason "error". The ShiftReport hold does send a packet (kind="shiftreport", per participant, line 1351) immediately before it, but "shiftreport" is absent from the client's KNOWN_KINDS in the mirror, so it renders nothing and the screen simply holds the previous final-score board for 5 extra seconds — dead air, not a blank screen. The podium beat was deleted (lines 1373-1379) but Podium.luau is still required at line 45 and never called, Pacing.Timing.Podium is orphaned, and — critically — the client's SHIFT COMPLETE end card (the PLAY AGAIN / BACK TO MENU rematch UI) is gated on receiving a kind=="podium" clear packet that nothing sends any more. Rematch is therefore not a vote at all: room.rematch only feeds a retention funnel, RoomService.carryReady is dead code, and the next session starts only when every seated member (including newly promoted bench players) presses READY.

nodes.role: The session spine. Owns preFlow (lobby presentation), runMatch (trial loop), runRoundGuarded (round watchdog) and the single finalizer. Started once from Main.server.luau:21.
Canonical single room, 2-4 players. Owns phase (Waiting/Starting/Playing/Aborting/Cleanup), sessionId, token, members, spectators, aborting flag, and the cancelled() predicate MachineFlow polls.
Session/Trial/Round/Leg token + cleanup-scope tree. MachineFlow creates the whole tree but never hands a scope to a trial module, so every scope it runs is empty (Gates 2/3/4 not done).
Shared arena/messaging kit. MachineFlow uses only TrialKit.abortRoom (watchdog teardown) and TrialKit.HOME_FALLBACK (the (0,5,0) teleport fallback).
Pure rules module: ROUNDS/LEGS per player count, RoundSeconds per trial, and the Pacing.Timing table every hold() reads.
Seeded shuffle (order/session/arrange). Consumed by runSelection (first trial) and playableOrder (the whole session order).
rankRound (tie-aware placement) and distribute (1700-point pool, doubled on the FINAL AUDIT).
Comment-line pool and the role-card sentence. One line rides every standings/score/final packet.
Playlist.TrialIds + PerSession=5 (gate 1 of the trial registry), Room.MinPlayers=2 / MaxPlayers=4 / RequireAllReady=true, Players.StudioTestMinimum=1, Match.StartCountdown=3.
ready=true trial 'birdhunt' / BIRD HUNTING. The only asymmetric one: MachineFlow forces the hunter seat and passes legIndex/legTotal. Exposes init, abort, runRound — NO cleanup.
ready=true trial 'minefield' / DEAD ZONE. Exposes init, abort, runRound — NO cleanup.
ready=true trial 'canteen' / CANTEEN PROTOCOL. The only trial exposing cleanup(ctx), so it is the only one MachineFlow tears down between trials and on abort.

The twelve MP-05 stubs (CutToSpec, ArmsIssue, Upstream, FloorCheck, Clearance, Carrier, Breather, ClearTheDeck, Crawler, Ricochet, PalletDuty, SortingFloor). All ready=false, all required at boot and all init()'d, none schedulable.
ORPHANED. Still required by MachineFlow:45; Podium.raise/strike/origin are called from nowhere outside this file.
LIVE. Resolves a fixed bench camera per trial; MachineFlow's benchCamera() sends packetFor(trialId) at Trial stage and clearPacket() when the trial ends or the session dies.
Volatile-first lifetime profiles. MachineFlow calls recordTrial (per trial), recordSession (per participant, returns the SHIFT REPORT receipt) and flush. Every call pcall-wrapped.
AnalyticsService wrapper. MachineFlow fires funnel steps 2/3/4/5 of KenopsiaRetention.
Six retention badges. checkSession is called once per participant straight off the Profiles receipt, pcall-wrapped.
Teleports the last remaining player to the menu place 129909297895850. Does NOT abort the match itself — that stays RoomService.abortMatch.
Server bootstrap; requires and starts MachineFlow with RoomService as the only injected dependency.
The client monolith that dispatches MachineState packets. MIRROR IS KNOWN STALE — every client claim below is marked NEEDS_RUNTIME.
Separate LocalScript. Any LobbyError message beginning 'RUN ABORTED' blacks the screen and freezes input for 5 s.
ReplicatedStorage.Kenopsia.Remotes.MachineState, created (or adopted) by MachineFlow.start:1419-1425. Every tell/tellRoom/tellBench packet goes down this one RemoteEvent. Never FireAllClients.
Broadcasts publicState (phase, stage, members, spectators, trial/round/leg progress) to every player on every state change.
Per-player rejection channel. abortMatch is the only sender that prefixes 'RUN ABORTED - '.
RoomReadyRequest. The ONLY reachable rematch input: the lobby Btn_READY toggle.
{kind='selection', icons(3), chosen(1-3), name}. Sent twice per session shape: preFlow:471 (lobby) and the trial loop:951 (every trial change except trial 1 when room.preShown).
{kind='info', id, name, icon, index, total}. preFlow:481, trial loop:963, and the late-joiner watchdog:1489. index/total are not read by the mirror client.
{kind='status', lines[], line?}. Carries the briefing (969), the inter-round standings (1165), the trial score board (1226) and the bench 'A CYCLE IS IN PROGRESS' card (1467).
{kind='round', n, total, verbs}. Line 1011, one per round.
{kind='rolecard', text, seconds}. Line 1024. Bird Hunting only, and only when #room.members >= 2.
{kind='hide'}. Line 1029 (before the pre-round cover) and line 825 (cleanup, every exit route).
{kind='cover', hold=true, maxSeconds=Pacing.Timing.BlackoutMax=25}. Lines 1044 (pre-round, hides the teleport/arena build) and 1145 (post-round blackout).
{kind='score', board=final, final=true, line}. Line 1271. Sent EXACTLY ONCE per session, at FinalScore.

{kind='shiftreport', xpDelta, xpTotal, clearance, clearanceName, clearanceUp, streak, sessions, viable, bestBand, questsCompleted, fragments, keys, volatile, openSeats}. Lines 1351-1367, per participant, sent BEFORE the 5 s hold.
MachineCam audience packet or its clear. Bench-only (tellBench), never sent to participants.
DEAD PRODUCER. The client still handles kind=='podium' (2907) and gates the SHIFT COMPLETE end card on its clear form (3295-3301), but no server code sends it since the podium beat was removed.
Lines 750-785. Runs trial.module.runRound on a spawned thread under a budget of Pacing.RoundSeconds[id] + ROUND_OVERHEAD(15) + ROUND_GRACE(20). Polls both the deadline and room.aborting every 0.1 s.
runRoundGuarded return case 1 (line 784, `return ok, result`): the round thread finished. ok = the pcall status of runRound; result = its scores table, or the error message when ok is false.
runRoundGuarded return case 2 (line 782): (false, 'timeout') — the budget expired and room.aborting is false. Consumed as a soft failure.
runRoundGuarded return case 3 (line 782): (false, 'aborted') — room.aborting went true mid-round. Consumed as a FATAL error, indistinguishable at the call site from a genuine trial crash.
Finalizer value 1 (initial, line 791). Survives only if ok and (scoresCommitted or not cancelled). Does nothing but become the cleanupToWaiting print reason.
Finalizer value 2 (line 1392). Set only when ok AND outcome=='completed' AND not scoresCommitted AND ctx.cancelled(). No abort call; only the cleanupToWaiting print reason.

unfinished.what: A player-cancellation is routed through the ERROR branch. runRoundGuarded returns (false, "aborted") only when room.aborting is true, and the ONLY producer of room.aborting is RoomService.abortMatch — reached from removeMember when a participant leaves and the survivors fall below requiredMinimum. Both call sites treat any non-"timeout" second value as fatal and re-raise it, so a player leaving mid-round makes outcome = "error" and reaches RoomServiceRef.abort(room, "MINIGAME ERROR") at line 1398. PROOF THAT IT CANNOT SHOW: RoomService.abort -> abortMatch's first guard is `if room.phase ~= "Playing" and room.phase ~= "Starting" then return false end`, and room.phase was set to "Aborting" at RoomService.luau:243 in the same resumption (no yield) as the room.aborting = true at :242 that the watchdog observed. Nothing sets phase back to Playing before the finalizer: the only writer is beginCountdown (RoomService.luau:303), which needs phase == "Waiting", i.e. toWaiting, i.e. the cleanupToWaiting call that comes AFTER line 1398. So the MINIGAME ERROR abort is always a no-op on this route — no second LobbyError, no second warn from RoomService. The real damage is a mislabelled log (`[MachineFlow] session S… failed: aborted` + a debug.traceback) and cleanupToWaiting("error") printing `[RoomService] cleanup (error)` for what is a normal player quit.

risks: HARD LOCK IN THE LOBBY, NO TIMEOUT. After a session, toWaiting() clears every ready flag (RoomService.luau:222 `clearReady()`), and the next session needs Config.Room.RequireAllReady = true plus allReady() over ALL seated members (RoomService.luau:311-316). A single seated player who never presses READY blocks the room forever: there is no rematch timer, RoomLeaveRequest is a deliberate no-op that only re-broadcasts state (RoomService.luau:608-611), and promoteSpectators() has just added every bench player as a full member who must also ready up (RoomService.luau:186-194, called from toWaiting at :221). Rematch is therefore unanimous over the CURRENT seat list, not over the last session's participants.

runRoundGuarded cannot distinguish a watchdog timeout from a trial that errors with the literal string "timeout". MachineFlow.luau:1111/1118 compare the second return value against "timeout" by equality, and case 1 (line 784 `return ok, result`) puts a raw pcall error message in that same slot. A trial raising error("timeout") would be silently swallowed as a soft round cut instead of aborting the match.

The Bird Hunting hunter seat is chosen from the LIVE room.members, not from the frozen participant snapshot: `hunter = room.members[(roundIndex - 1) % #room.members + 1]` (MachineFlow.luau:1023). With 4 players, one leaving mid-trial keeps the match alive (requiredMinimum is min(#members, 2) = 2) but re-indexes the rotation, so a seat can be served twice or skipped. Everything else in the loop — scoring, standings, the final board — uses ctx.participantUserIds, which is snapshotted once at MachineFlow.luau:298-301.

Only CanteenProtocol exposes a cleanup(ctx); BirdHunting and Minefield expose only abort(). module.abort is called ONLY on the watchdog/abort route inside runRoundGuarded (MachineFlow.luau:778-780). If the session is cancelled during a hold() rather than during a round, cleanup() at :809-811 calls activeTrial.module.cleanup, which is nil for those two, and the Contexts scopes it runs are empty — so nothing in this file tears their arena down on that route.

In Studio, minPlayers() returns Config.Players.StudioTestMinimum = 1 (RoomService.luau:93-98), so requiredMinimum becomes 1 and removeMember never aborts. The whole "aborted" -> outcome="error" path is therefore INVISIBLE in Studio testing and only appears in a live server. Any play test of this finding must be run live, or with StudioTestMinimum temporarily at 2.

hold() polls at 0.1 s and calls task.wait(0.1) after each check, so every hold overshoots its Pacing value slightly and a cancellation is observed up to ~100 ms late (MachineFlow.luau:355-362). The one wait that is NOT cancellation-aware is preFlow's `task.wait(Pacing.Timing.LobbyReveal or 6.4)` at line 479 — a countdown starting during those 6.4 s is caught only by the phase guard at line 480 afterwards.

ctx.audience is a snapshot of Player INSTANCES taken once at match start (MachineFlow.luau:297 via RoomService.audience). tell(), setActiveTrial() and setTrialId() all iterate it and filter on `plr.Parent == Players`. A participant who disconnects and rejoins the same server within the session gets a new Player instance and would receive no further Machine packets and no attribute writes for the rest of that session.

A watchdog-cut round still counts toward the XP math: roundsRun += 1 at MachineFlow.luau:1151 executes before `if timedOut then break end` at :1159, and roundsRun is what Profiles.recordSession receives as roundsPlayed (:1304).
uncertainties: NEEDS_RUNTIME — everything I state about the client is [SOURCE] from studio-src/StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/KenopsiaClient.client.luau, which the task brief flags as BEHIND the live place. The predicted signature is, in order: `[RoomService] aborting match: PLAYER LEFT - CANNOT CONTINUE WITH A SINGLE PLAYER`, then `[MachineFlow] <trial> round cut by match abort`, then `[MachineFlow] session S… failed: aborted` with a traceback, then `[RoomService] cleanup (error)` — and NO second `aborting match: MINIGAME ERROR` line and no second RUN ABORTED card. If a `MINIGAME ERROR` line does appear, my no-op proof is wrong and there is a phase window I did not find.

maps.area: Client side of the server→client packet contract — KenopsiaClient, MachineLayout, SocialClient, AbortScreen, ReplicatedFirst/KenopsiaLoading, Shared/Net/Envelope (MainGame, placeId 110672791536316)
maps.summary: The whole client is driven by ONE RemoteEvent, `ReplicatedStorage.Kenopsia.Remotes.MachineState`, carrying a flat `{kind = "..."}` union; four separate LocalScripts each open their own `OnClientEvent` on it (KenopsiaClient's main dispatch, KenopsiaClient's own end-card block, SocialClient, RunnerClient, SonarClient). KenopsiaClient dispatches 28 kinds through a hand-written if-chain, then a whitelist `K.KNOWN_KINDS` (8 screen kinds) gates the screen funnel; anything unrecognised is warned once and dropped. [RUNTIME] I reached the live place through the weppy bridge (clientId ad22f53b-…, placeId 110672791536316, studioState "edit") and read live source directly, so the known mirror staleness is resolved for every claim below — and it mattered: the mirror is missing the live `feed`, `hud` and `fieldPush` handlers entirely. The live set difference is small and exact: SENT BUT NOT HANDLED = `shiftreport`, `profilestate`, `emotestate` (all three server-authored as deliberately "ships dark"); HANDLED BUT NEVER SENT = `mines` and `podium`, plus `trial` which is handled by a full router + 12 client modules that can never fire because all twelve TrialKit trials are `ready = false`. The removed podium beat is load-bearing in the worst way: the SHIFT COMPLETE end card — the only PLAY AGAIN / BACK TO MENU affordance in the game — is gated behind a `podium` CLEAR packet that no server code can produce, so it is dead UI. There is no return-to-menu path on the client at all: [RUNTIME] zero `TeleportService` references across all 26 live StarterPlayerScripts. KenopsiaLoading is bounded except for two unbounded yields (`game.Loaded:Wait()` and `ContentProvider:PreloadAsync`) and pays a guaranteed 10 s `WaitForChild("Warning", 10)` that can never succeed because the `Warning` frame does not exist; KenopsiaClient pays the same 10 s again at top level. SocialClient fires the Roblox invite sheet on `shiftreport` — which lands exactly 6 s into the final standings card, over results that are still on screen. `Shared/Net/Envelope` is dead: [RUNTIME] across 115 live scripts nothing requires it.

nodes.role: The monolith. Owns the single MachineState if-chain dispatch (live 3419-3745), every machine screen, the camera writer, sniper/canteen/minefield input, the LobbyError notice, and a SECOND MachineState listener for the SHIFT COMPLETE end card (live 4108).

risks: BOOT COST: every join pays a guaranteed 10 s WaitForChild for a frame that cannot appear, twice. LIVE KenopsiaLoading:254 sits BEFORE the PreloadAsync block, so the bridge holds 10 s longer than intended before it even starts preloading. LIVE KenopsiaClient:3751 is worse — it is a top-level statement, so all 374 lines after it (settings panel wiring, the LobbyError notice at ~4023, the '[Kenopsia] client online' print, and the end-card listener at 4108) are deferred by the full timeout. They run on different scripts so they overlap rather than sum, but both fire every join.

LOADING SCREEN CAN STRAND WITH NO ENGINE FALLBACK. KenopsiaLoading:12 calls ReplicatedFirst:RemoveDefaultLoadingScreen(), and [RUNTIME] `done` is assigned true at exactly ONE place (LIVE KenopsiaLoading:282, the last line of the second coroutine, weppy search 'done' → 6 hits, one assignment). The ledger coroutine is `while not done do` (LIVE:234). If the second coroutine errors anywhere between line 242 and 282 — and it has NO pcall around the WaitForChilds or the `machineGui.Enabled = true` write — the dots loop runs forever behind a screen nothing will ever destroy. Two unbounded yields sit in that window: `game.Loaded:Wait()` (LIVE:245, no timeout) and `ContentProvider:PreloadAsync` (unbounded; the pcall catches a throw, not a hang).

THE INVITE SHEET LANDS ON TOP OF THE RESULTS, BY DESIGN. MachineFlow.luau:1271 puts the final board up, :1330 holds 6.0 s (Pacing FinalScore), :1346-1370 fires shiftreport, :1371 holds another 5.0 s. SocialClient:84 calls promptInvite() straight off that packet. So Roblox's invite sheet opens at t+6 s over a standings card that stays on screen for another 5 s — and since nothing renders shiftreport, the popup is the ONLY thing that changes in that window. SocialClient's own header (:12-13) argues this is the honest moment ("the numbers are on screen, everyone is still here"); whether a modal over the verdict is what was wanted is a design call, but it is not an accident and it is not avoidable from the client.

FIVE SCRIPTS SHARE ONE UNVERSIONED PACKET UNION. MachineState carries 29 kinds with no schema, no version field, and five independent OnClientEvent handlers (KenopsiaClient x2, SocialClient, RunnerClient, SonarClient). Every listener re-tests `p.kind` from scratch. The project has already been bitten by this — KenopsiaClient:318-320 records that `kind = "select"` once cancelled every typewriter mid-word — and the current mitigation is one warn-once per unknown kind (LIVE:3703-3709), which is a log line, not a gate. UNGUARDED VECTOR INDEXING IN THE SPECTATE PATH. LIVE KenopsiaClient:3465-3466 — "local pos = Vector3.new(p.pos[1], p.pos[2], p.pos[3]) / local look = Vector3.new(p.look[1], p.look[2], p.look[3])" with no nil check. maps.area: Kenopsia MainGame (placeId 110672791536316) — the three ENABLED trials (BIRD HUNTING / DEAD ZONE / CANTEEN PROTOCOL) and the trial framework (MachineFlow registry, TrialKit, Contexts, Playlist, TrialRules, Scoring, Pacing)
maps.summary: The trial registry is a two-gate system: an id must appear in GameConfig.Playlist.TrialIds AND its MachineFlow TRIALS entry must declare ready = true; 3 of 15 pass both gates today (birdhunt, minefield, canteen), and I confirmed the same 3-true/12-false pattern in the live place. [SOURCE + RUNTIME] The framework has split in two: TrialKit's Round object (place/countdown/tick/kill/scores/endRound/cleanup) is the contract for the twelve MP-05 trials, but NONE of the three enabled trials require it — BirdHunting, Minefield and CanteenProtocol each hand-roll their own livingOf/announce/countdown/scoring, so the shared framework is exercised in production only by disabled stubs. Round lifecycle in TrialKit is newRound (registry + guard armed before any yield) -> place (freeze at spawn, mark bodyless members done) -> begin -> countdown (3-2-1, opens input, arms deadline) -> tick (0.05 s loop bounded by deadline and a +20 s failsafe) -> scores -> endRound (cover + 0.6 s) -> cleanup (idempotent, LIFO, unregister-first, restore humanoids, teleport home). Bird Hunting's hunter is picked in MachineFlow, not in BirdHunting: `room.members[(roundIndex - 1) % #room.members + 1]`, always starting at index 1, over exactly 3 legs for every player count — so with 4 players the fourth roster slot (deterministically the 4th player to join, since members is append-order) NEVER hunts, and Bird Hunting is played at most once per session. There is NO per-trial teaching text triggered for a first-time player: the only per-trial instruction is the CONTROLS window inside the lobby Info panel (MachineLayout.TRIAL_TEXT), plus a 5-line status card of the trial name + tagline; the two-page BRIEFING screen is an opt-in main-menu panel that no trial flow ever opens. The hunter is chosen in MachineFlow, not in BirdHunting: [SOURCE+RUNTIME] MachineFlow.luau:1023 `hunter = room.members[(roundIndex - 1) % #room.members + 1]` — confirmed byte-identical at line 1023 of the LIVE MachineFlow. It ALWAYS starts from member index 1 (roundIndex begins at 1, so the first term is 0 % n + 1 = 1). Leg count is fixed at 3 for every player count: Pacing.luau:60 `local LEGS = { [2] = 3, [3] = 3, [4] = 3 }` (confirmed live at line 60), reached via MachineFlow.luau:988 `local rounds = Pacing.roundsFor(trial.id, playerCount)` and Pacing.luau:63-64 `if trialId == "birdhunt" then return row(LEGS, playerCount)`. Working it out: 2 PLAYERS (n=2): leg1 -> (1-1)%2+1 = 1; leg2 -> (2-1)%2+1 = 2; leg3 -> (3-1)%2+1 = 1. Members [1,2,1] — member 1 hunts TWICE, member 2 once. Nobody denied, but the split is 2:1. 3 PLAYERS (n=3): leg1 -> 0%3+1 = 1; leg2 -> 1%3+1 = 2; leg3 -> 2%3+1 = 3. Members [1,2,3] — exactly one hunt each, the only fair case. 4 PLAYERS (n=4): leg1 -> 0%4+1 = 1; leg2 -> 1%4+1 = 2; leg3 -> 2%4+1 = 3. Members [1,2,3] — MEMBER 4 IS NEVER THE HUNTER. There is no second chance: Playlist.order permutes each id exactly once (Playlist.luau:53 `-- Fisher-Yates. Every id exactly once, no repeats`), so BIRD HUNTING runs at most once per session. And the denied slot is not random: room.members is append-on-join and never shuffled (RoomService.luau:44 `members = {},        -- ordered: { userId, displayName, ready }`; :172 `table.insert(room.members, {`), so it is deterministically the 4th player to sit down. BirdHunting's own fallback rotation (BirdHunting.luau:480-481, live 481-482) is identical in shape and only reached on a direct/solo call.

SCORE CONSEQUENCE OF THE DENIED SLOT. A hunter leg is worth far more than a runner leg, so slot 4's ceiling is roughly half everyone else's. Hunter: [SOURCE] BirdHunting.luau:1518 `scores[uid] = math.min(st.points, DETAIL_CAP)` with DETAIL_CAP 999 (:92) and a stated legit maximum of 745 (:91 `-- 3 x 115 (345) + Birds x BirdDetail (400) = 745`). Runner: :1520 `scores[uid] = 100 + math.floor((st.escapeTimeLeft or 0) * 2)` where escapeTimeLeft <= ROUND_TIME = 60 (:1389, :29), so <= 220 per leg; a timed-out runner gets :1522 `scores[uid] = math.floor(st.progress * 100)` (<= 100) and a dead runner :1524 `scores[uid] = 0`. Three legs: members 1-3 can reach ~745 + 2x220 = 1185; member 4 can reach at most 3x220 = 660. Those totals are what MachineFlow ranks (:1149 `trialTotals[uid] = (trialTotals[uid] or 0) + value`, :1182-1185), so the 4th-to-join player is structurally placed lower in BIRD HUNTING's 1700-point distribution.

DETAIL POINTS CAN EXCEED 999 — in DEAD ZONE, and only there. The framework contract is TrialRules.luau:29-37: `TrialRules.BAND = { FINISHED = 2000, ALIVE = 1000, OUT = 0 }`, `TrialRules.BAND_WIDTH = 1000`, and key() clamps: `if d > TrialRules.BAND_WIDTH - 1 then d = TrialRules.BAND_WIDTH - 1 end`. No enabled trial calls it (grep TrialRules.key / TrialKit.key across the three enabled modules: zero hits; the only callers are the MP-05 stubs, e.g. CutToSpec.luau:63). CANTEEN re-implements it correctly — CanteenProtocol.luau:174-176 (`ELIMINATED_BAND = 0` / `ALIVE_BAND = 1000` / `FINISHED_BAND = 2000`), :182 `local DETAIL_CAP = 999`, and all three branches clamp (:1343 `key = FINISHED_BAND + math.min(DETAIL_CAP, math.floor(spare * FINISH_SPEED_STEP))`, :1345, :1349) — max key 2999, detail never above 999. BIRD HUNTING uses no bands at all: its four score branches (:1518-1524) are raw numbers, so 'FINISHED > ALIVE > OUT' is not enforced there — a timed-out runner at full progress (100) outranks a hunter who hit nothing (0). DEAD ZONE BREAKS THE 999 RULE: Minefield.luau:1513-1515 `local ESCAPE_BAND = 2000` / `local ORDER_STEP = 100` / `local DETAIL_CAP = 999`, then :1522-1523 `sc = ESCAPE_BAND + math.max(0, 1000 - ORDER_STEP * ((ps.escapeOrder or 1) - 1))` — the FIRST escapee gets detail exactly 1000, and DETAIL_CAP is applied only on the eliminated branch (:1527 `sc = math.min(detail, DETAIL_CAP)`). Then :1531 `if not ps.usedScanner then sc += 1 end` runs for EVERYONE including escapees, so the true maximum is 2000 + 1000 + 1 = 3001, i.e. detail 1001. Inside Dead Zone alone nothing is corrupted (there is no band above 2000), and the comment at :1499 half-acknowledges it (`escaped       2000 + 1000 down to 2000`) — but the +1 pushing it past the band width is not acknowledged anywhere, and any future trial that stacks a band above 2000 while reusing this pattern would silently cross it.

SUMMING ORDERING KEYS ACROSS ROUNDS is arithmetically unsafe and is what the session actually does. MachineFlow.luau:1149 `trialTotals[uid] = (trialTotals[uid] or 0) + value` adds banded keys, then :1182-1183 ranks on `a.raw > b.raw`. CanteenProtocol.luau:158-159 states the design (`runRound returns one ordering key per player and MachineFlow sums those across rounds`), but summing bands is not order-preserving: in a 3-round DEAD ZONE, escaping SECOND three times (2900+1 each = 8703) beats escaping FIRST twice and dying once (3001+3001+1 = 6003). Consistency beats peaks by construction — defensible as a design, but it is nowhere written down as one, and no test covers it.

TRIALINPUT IS ONE REMOTE WITH FOUR INDEPENDENT SERVER HANDLERS, each with its own hand-written validation ladder: TrialKit.luau:387 (12-step, the strict one), Minefield.luau:452, CanteenProtocol.luau:923, BirdHunting.luau:196. Only TrialKit's ladder enforces per-player/per-action rate limiting (:420 `if now < (ps.lastInput[action] or 0) + (sp.perAction[action] or sp.cooldown) then return end`) and the NaN-seq guard (:413 `if payload.seq ~= payload.seq then return end`); the three enabled trials each re-derive their own subset (BirdHunting's is only :213-216: active / phase / roundToken). Any future hardening of the ladder has to be applied four times or it is not applied at all.

A PLAYER WITH NO LIVING CHARACTER is handled four different ways. TrialKit (disabled trials): Round:place marks them done and gives no feedback at all — TrialKit.luau:588-589 `if not s then` / `if ps then ps.done = true end`; they are then skipped by countdown (:562-563) and by kill/out (:733, :762), and Round:scores zero-fills over room.members (:775-779). DEAD ZONE: Minefield.luau:760 `state[mm.userId] = { done = s == nil, escaped = false, progress = 0, usedScanner = false, ...}` — done, progress 0, and then :1531 `if not ps.usedScanner then sc += 1 end` awards them the clean-run tiebreaker, so a player who was never in the round scores 1 and outranks a live player who used the sonar and made no progress (0). CANTEEN: CanteenProtocol.luau:1099 `finished = false, finishing = false, eliminated = s == nil,` -> scored 0 (:1349 with eliminatedAt nil -> survived 0). BIRD HUNTING: the state entry is created with `done = isSniper` (BirdHunting.luau:664), so a bodyless RUNNER is not done at creation and is only dropped on the first main-loop tick (:1446-1449 `elseif not st.sniper then` / `st.done = true`). MachineFlow mitigates all of this by force-respawning before every round (:1076-1081 `pcall(function() plr:LoadCharacter() end)`) and waiting — but the wait uses a key that does not exist: :1082 `local deadline = os.clock() + (Pacing.Timing.RespawnGrace or 5)` and Pacing.Timing (Pacing.luau:120-183) has no RespawnGrace field, so this is a silent constant 5, not a tunable.

THE ONLY PER-TRIAL INSTRUCTION IS VISIBLE FOR ~3.5 SECONDS BETWEEN TRIALS. The CONTROLS window lives inside the lobby Info panel (MachineLayout.client.luau:333 `local cw = info and info:FindFirstChild("ControlsWindow")`; confirmed live at game.StarterGui.KenopsiaMachine.Info.ControlsWindow), and Info is shown only by showInfo (KenopsiaClient.client.luau:2199 `info.Visible = true`), which every other card's hideAll() closes. In the lobby it stays up until READY is pressed (preFlow sends the info packet at MachineFlow.luau:481-486 and then waits for readiness) — so the FIRST trial's controls can be read at leisure. Between trials it is up for exactly Pacing.Timing.Reveal = 3.5 s (MachineFlow.luau:963-965; Pacing.luau:121), competing with a typewriter animation, and the 8-second BRIEFING card that follows (:969-976, ControlCard = 8.0) shows the status screen, which does NOT contain the controls window. So trials 2 and 3 are effectively unbriefed.
uncertainties: EXACT VERBATIM TEXT A PLAYER IS TOLD BEFORE EACH TRIAL — server side is certain, client rendering is not. From source, the sequence per trial is: (1) roulette card {kind='selection', name=<displayName>}; (2) info card 'NEXT SIMULATION: <displayName>' (KenopsiaClient.client.luau:2214 `typewrite(info.NextLabel, "NEXT SIMULATION: " .. (p.name or "?"), ...)`) with the CONTROLS window beside it; (3) the BRIEFING status card, MachineFlow.luau:969-975, five lines: `trial.displayName`, `trial.tagline`, `" "`, `isFinal and "FINAL AUDIT. DOUBLE WEIGHT." or ("Minigame %d of %d."):format(trialIndex, #order)`, `"Bootstrapping simulation ..."`; (4) the round card {kind='round', verbs = trial.tagline} (:1011-1012); (5) Bird Hunting only, the role card '<NAME> IS THE HUNTER.' (:1024-1026 + MachineVoice.luau:126); (6) the trial's own one-line announce. VERBATIM PER TRIAL — BIRD HUNTING: displayName 'BIRD HUNTING' (MachineFlow.luau:82), tagline 'CROSS THE FIELD. THE TOWER IS LOADED.' (:87), unused subtitle 'THE SIGHTLINE NEVER BLINKS._' (:84), controls sec1 'RUNNERS:' sec2 'HUNTER:' with Desktop rows 'Move  [{Move}]' / 'Crouch [{Crouch}]' / 'Aim + Shoot [{Fire}]' / 'Scope [{Scope}]  x2 / x4 [{Zoom}]' and scoring page 'Headshot     instant  +100' / 'Body shot    2 to drop' / 'Winged       +15 / kill +60' / 'Escape       +100 & time' / 'Timeout      distance only' (MachineLayout.client.luau:133-162); in-trial announce SKIPPED in every real session (BirdHunting.luau:644 `if not forcedHunterUserId then`). KEEP MOVING._' (:96), controls sec1 'RUNNERS:' sec2 'SONAR:' rows 'Move  [{Move}]' / 'Use sonar [HOLD {Scan}]' with an EMPTY scoring page `scoring = {}` (MachineLayout.client.luau:164-187), in-trial announce 'MARK THE GROUND. OUTRUN THE PRESS.' (Minefield.luau:658 — the same sentence as the tagline, so the player is told one thing twice and the mine mechanic never). EAT ONLY WHEN UNOBSERVED._' (:120), controls sec1 'DINERS:' sec2 'OBSERVER:' rows 'Seated - no moving' / 'Load fork [{Load}]' / 'Swallow [{Swallow}]' / 'Never swallow while watched' plus a second page 'Plate         16 rations' / 'Fork          holds 4' / 'Loading       always safe' / 'Swallowing    only unobserved' / 'Finish first  ranks highest' (MachineLayout.client.luau:195-225), in-trial announce 'EAT EVERYTHING. DO NOT BE SEEN.' (CanteenProtocol.luau:1198). NEEDS_RUNTIME: the KenopsiaClient repo copy is known-stale, so whether these strings actually render (and for how long) must be settled by a play test — the observation that would settle it is a 4-player play test with a screen recording of the Info panel from the {kind='info'} packet to the {kind='status'} briefing card, checking that ControlsWindow.Row1..Row3 are populated and legible and that Page2 is reachable for canteen.

That is consistent with Page2/PageLabel being hidden for minefield (KenopsiaClient.client.luau:3074 gates the second page on `TrialId == "canteen"` only), but whether the client leaves stale rows on screen from a previous trial is NEEDS_RUNTIME — applyControlsText only writes `trial.scoring[i] or ""` into p2.R1..R5 (:1092), which should blank them, but p2.Visible is owned by KenopsiaClient's renderPage and the repo copy is stale.

maps.summary: The entire analytics surface of Kenopsia is ONE module (Services/Telemetry.luau) wrapping two engine calls, five funnel-step firings, and exactly one custom event. [RUNTIME] weppy manage_scripts search over the live MainGame place (placeId 110672791536316, 115 scripts searched) found "AnalyticsService" in exactly one script — Telemetry — at lines 4/17/93/104, and "TelemetryEvent" in exactly two scripts (LightGuard:60, Telemetry:9/136/139); live line numbers match the repo mirror byte-for-byte, so the KNOWN HAZARD does not apply to this area. The funnel is "KenopsiaRetention": 1 Joined (Profiles.luau:261), 2 RouletteSeen (MachineFlow.luau:476), 3 Round1Done (MachineFlow.luau:1156), 4 VerdictSeen (MachineFlow.luau:1327), 5 RematchAccepted (MachineFlow.luau:505). There is ONE custom event, "MobileBlackScreen", and no server code ever calls Telemetry.event — the only path to LogCustomEvent is the client remote (Telemetry.luau:128), whitelisted to that single name (Telemetry.luau:27-29). Three named metrics are dishonest as written: "Joined" is gated behind the DataStore load and its retry backoff, so a player who bounces in the first ~7-95 s produces NO event at all — the exact bounce cohort the MASTERPLAN names as the primary ranking signal; "RematchAccepted" is not acceptance but "was a verdict participant, is still seated 6.4 s into the next lobby roulette, and did not explicitly press un-ready", and it is structurally SKIPPED for the players who accept fastest; "MobileBlackScreen" is a device+quality heuristic (touch device AND SavedQualityLevel <= 4, where 0/Automatic is the mobile default) with no pixel evidence whatsoever. There is NO per-match session identifier anywhere in analytics: LogFunnelStepEvent's funnelSessionId argument is hard-coded nil (Telemetry.luau:104) even though RoomService mints a real room.sessionId at RoomService.luau:297. The menu place Kenopsia_DEV (129909297895850, dev-src/) — the actual front door, where parties form before teleporting into a reserved MainGame server — has zero telemetry of any kind. The plan document promises a 6-step funnel and 6 custom events; 5 of the 6 events and 1 of the 6 steps do not exist in code.

risks: 'Joined' HIDES EARLY EXITS — PROVEN FROM SOURCE. Telemetry.funnel(plr, FUNNEL, 1, "Joined") sits at Profiles.luau:261, which is reached only after the DataStore load loop (Profiles.luau:227-258). Three guards return without firing it: :232 (+:239 return) 'left while we were loading', :252 after a backoff wait, and :258 immediately before the fire. With LOAD_ATTEMPTS=3 and LOAD_BACKOFF={2,5} (Profiles.luau:42-43) a failing or throttled store costs at minimum 7 s of task.wait plus three UpdateAsync round trips; a 'locked by another server' result (Profiles.luau:124 "return nil, \"locked by another server\"") is treated as a plain failure and runs the full retry path even though it will never succeed within LOCK_STALE_SECONDS=180. Meanwhile the boot watchdog holds joiners out for 7 s (MachineFlow.luau:1455 "if os.clock() - plr:GetAttribute(\"KenopsiaJoinedAt\") > 7") and Profiles.GREETING_DELAY=8 (Profiles.luau:48) — i.e. the first ~8 s are a black content-warning screen. A player who bounces in exactly that window produces NO funnel event at all. The published bounce number will therefore be systematically optimistic, and MASTERPLAN.md:291's 'bounce < 60 s' gate is not measurable by this instrumentation.

'RematchAccepted' MEASURES SEAT OCCUPANCY, NOT ACCEPTANCE — and is INVERTED for the fastest accepters. room.rematch enrolls every verdict participant unconditionally (MachineFlow.luau:1279-1281 "for _, uid in ctx.participantUserIds do rematchIds[uid] = true end" / "room.rematch = { userIds = rematchIds, until_ = os.clock() + 60 }"). The only removal is an explicit un-ready press (RoomService.luau:365-366). The fire at MachineFlow.luau:505 is gated on :501 "if rematch and os.clock() < rematch.until_ then" and :503 "if rematch.userIds[m.userId] then" — i.e. still enrolled, still a member, inside 60 s. The code's own comment admits it: MachineFlow.luau:496-497 "Das Funnel feuert weiterhin: wer nach dem Verdikt sitzen geblieben ist, zaehlt als Rematch-Interesse" ('whoever stayed seated after the verdict counts as rematch interest'). An AFK player counts as an acceptance. Worse: since 30.08.2026 removed carryReady, acceptance is a manual READY press, and if all seated members press READY during the 6.4 s LobbyReveal wait, RoomService.luau:278 sets phase='Starting' and MachineFlow.luau:480 "if room.phase ~= \"Waiting\" or #room.members == 0 then return end" returns before line 505 — the players who most enthusiastically accepted the rematch are the ones EXCLUDED from the metric. The step name is the opposite of the behaviour.

'MobileBlackScreen' IS A MOBILE-PLAYER COUNTER, NOT A BLACK-SCREEN COUNTER. The two conditions are LightGuard.client.luau:33 "if not UserInputService.TouchEnabled then return end" and :39 "if quality == nil or quality > CONFIG.LowQualityMax then return end" with LowQualityMax=4 (:19) and the explicit note :40 "-- 0 is Automatic, 1..4 the low tiers -- both count as at-risk". SavedQualityLevel=Automatic(0) is the default for any player who never opened settings, so on touch devices the predicate is close to always-true. There is no luminance read, no frame sample, no Lighting inspection — the header says so at :7-9 "it fires on the heuristic, not on a proven black frame; the name is kept for the analytics counter". It also fires AFTER the mitigation is applied (:51-55 raise the ambient floor, :57-69 then report), so even a client that was successfully fixed is counted. The name is misleading and the counter will be read as a bug rate when it is a device census. [RUNTIME] the live LocalScript is byte-identical to the repo file, so this is not a mirror-lag artifact.

NO PER-MATCH SESSION IDENTIFIER ANYWHERE IN ANALYTICS. Telemetry.luau:104 passes nil for funnelSessionId, and Telemetry.funnel's signature (Telemetry.luau:100) has no slot for one, so no call site could supply it. RoomService.luau:297 already mints room.sessionId ('S%d-%d') and MachineFlow logs it in warnings (:1397), but it never reaches AnalyticsService. Consequence: with one-time-funnel semantics, everything after a player's first traversal is deduped — you can learn 'this player ever finished a first round' but never 'how many matches per visit', 'did session 3 convert better than session 1', or 'how many rematches happened'. Every session by the same player is conflated by construction.

ONE-TIME AND PER-MATCH SEMANTICS ARE MIXED IN A SINGLE FUNNEL. Step 1 (Joined) is per-server-join, and because every match runs on a freshly reserved server teleported in from the menu (dev-src PlaylistService.luau:166-169), it is effectively per-party-teleport. Steps 2/3/4 are per-match code that re-executes on every session in that server (MachineFlow.luau:1407-1410 respawns preFlow after each match). Step 5 is by definition a second-session event. All five are logged into the same nil-session funnel, so the recurring steps silently collapse to their first occurrence. The developers half-know this — MachineFlow.luau:472-473 "One-time funnel -- Analytics dedupes repeats per player" — but the funnel is named 'KenopsiaRetention' and is expected (docs/INNER-GAME-PLAN.md:248-249) to make retention gates measurable, which a deduped one-time funnel cannot do.

STEP SKIPS PRODUCE IMPOSSIBLE CONVERSION RATES. Step 2 iterates room.members at preFlow time (MachineFlow.luau:474-477) while steps 3 and 4 iterate ctx.participantUserIds, snapshotted at countdown (RoomService.luau:298-299). A player who takes a seat after preFlow has already run gets steps 3 and 4 with no step 2, which will render as a >100% step2->step3 conversion. Conversely, solo players get step 2 and can never get step 3 (see unfinished item).

ANALYTICS FAILURE IS ITSELF INVISIBLE. Telemetry.luau:37-41 warnOnce is keyed on two constants only — 'event' (:96) and 'funnel' (:107) — so a universe where AnalyticsService is rejecting calls emits exactly two warnings for the entire server lifetime and then goes silent, with no dropped-event counter. Combined with the pcall wrappers at :92 and :103, a totally non-functioning analytics pipeline is indistinguishable from a healthy one in the server log.

BOOT-CRITICAL COUPLING IN THE ANALYTICS MODULE. Telemetry.luau:135 does two unbounded WaitForChild calls ("ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild(\"Kenopsia\"):WaitForChild(\"Remotes\")") on the main boot thread, at Main.server.luau:17 — before Profiles.start(), EmoteService.start(), CharacterService.start() and MachineFlow.start() (Main.server.luau:18-21), none of which are pcall-guarded. In practice RoomService.start() at :16 creates the folder synchronously (RoomService.luau:583 ensureRemotes -> :562-563), so this does not hang today; but any future reordering or partial failure of RoomService.start turns the analytics module into a total server-boot hang.

maps.summary: Fifteen trials are declared; exactly three are playable. Schedulability is gated twice and independently — an id must appear in `GameConfig.Playlist.TrialIds` AND its `MachineFlow` registry row must declare `ready = true`. [RUNTIME] The live place has ready=true on exactly three rows (MachineFlow lines 88/100/130) and ready=false on twelve. Eleven of the twelve are byte-shaped 75-line "FRAMEWORK STUB" files that play a compliant no-op round; the twelfth (SortingFloor) is fully built and deliberately held back until after release. This is designed dormancy, not breakage: every stub carries an explicit header saying so, and the two gates carry comments explaining why listing an id cannot leak it. BREATHER is the one dormant row with a content problem: its registry subtitle is `"ONE CIGARETTE. THIRTY SECONDS. NOTHING ELSE._"` and its full design in docs/MP-04 is a cigarette-smoking simulator (hold-to-inhale, ember, lung meter, cough, ashtray) — content Roblox does not permit at any maturity level. [RUNTIME] That string is the only occurrence of "CIGARETTE" across all 115 scripts in the live place, it is on a ready=false row, and no code anywhere reads the registry's `subtitle` field, so nothing reaches a player today. On the gore side the E6 "mild ~14+" decision cut blood volume to ~40% behind one `GORE` table, but it did NOT remove body destruction: `shatter()` still hides the whole body and spawns 5 chunk parts plus 2 leg-shaped chunk parts plus a blood fountain, and it is called on the second-mine death, the compactor death, and the Canteen execution. Both docs/INNER-GAME-PLAN.md and docs/RELEASE-CHECKLIST.md state "no dismemberment"; the shipped code's own comment on that function is "ZERSTUECKELUNG: der Koerper zerreisst komplett in Brocken". The checklist's item 6 asks the user to re-answer the Creator Hub age questionnaire DOWN on the strength of that claim, which the code does not support. Separately, [RUNTIME] confirmed the repo mirror studio-src/ is behind live: `BloodFX.mark` exists live at line 97 and is absent from the mirror, while `CanteenProtocol.luau:565` calls it — a Rojo push from studio-src today would break every Canteen execution.

reviews.reasoning:
Could not refute. I re-read Profiles.luau from scratch and independently re-verified live (weppy studio-2, placeId 110672791536316): _lock search returns exactly 5 hits at lines 91/100/118/138/140, trySave search returns 129/238/279/473/649, get_source 96-150 is byte-identical to the mirror, lineCount 663. The quoted evidence says what the verdict claims.

Core mechanics confirmed on both disk and live: lockHeldByOther (:99-104) is the ONLY read of _lock and is called only from tryLoad (:112); the only acquisition is :118 `data._lock = { jobId = game.JobId, ts = now }` — a per-SERVER identity, not a per-load token; trySave (:129-147) copies every OWNED_FIELDS key from the stale in-memory `data` over `stored` (:134-135) and then either nils the lock (:138) or re-stamps itself owner (:140), in both branches with no comparison against stored._lock.jobId, no early return, and no telemetry. The single pcall (:131) wraps the UpdateAsync for error suppression, not as a guard.

Refutation attempts that failed: (1) "UpdateAsync re-reads on conflict so the write isn't stale" — true but irrelevant; `stored` is always current, `data` (entry.data, :130) is the stale side, which is exactly why the missing in-transform check is load-bearing. (2) "A guard the first pass missed" — there IS one the first pass missed, Profiles.flush:472 `if live[entry.userId] ~= entry then return end`, but it is a local-liveness check evaluated BEFORE the UpdateAsync, not an ownership check inside the transform, and it exists on only one of four call sites. (3) "A wrapper/second lock service enforces ownership" — `grep -rln "jobId|JobId" --include=*.luau studio-src` returns exactly one file, Profiles.luau. (4) "The mirror is stale" — closed by the live re-verification above; Profiles is indeed not Rojo-mapped (`grep -n "Profiles" default.project.json` exits 1), so I did not rely on the mirror.

The verdict's precision correction (a marker exists, but it is per-server not per-load) is accurate and honest. All three parts of the claim hold: no unique per-load token; saves and releases verify nothing; a stale server can therefore overwrite or unlock a newer owner.

One supporting leg is overstated and should be relabelled, but it does not change the verdict: the finding cites EmoteService.luau:471-473 as [SOURCE] that DEV and MainGame both write KenopsiaProfile_v1. That is prose, not code — `grep -rn "DataStoreService|UpdateAsync|GetAsync|SetAsync" dev-src` hits only PartyRegistry.luau:56,90,114 (a party-code map), no profile store anywhere in dev-src's 22 files, and dev-src/.../UI/Theme.luau:120 says "No DataStore in the MVP by design". The reachability argument survives without that leg via crash/soft-shutdown plus rejoin, and via the :232-239 same-server race.
missedEvidence: Profiles.luau:232-239 is an INTRA-server instance of the same bug the first pass treated only as 'a write path'. Because :102 `if lock.jobId == game.JobId then return false end` treats a same-server lock as unowned, a player who leaves mid-load and rejoins the SAME server gets a new entry and a new tryLoad while the old loader thread still holds a snapshot and then fires `trySave(entry, true)` at :238 — overwrite plus unlock, with zero cross-server assumption. This is the cleanest proof that a per-LOAD token, not a per-server one, is what is missing.

Profiles.luau:472 `if live[entry.userId] ~= entry then return end -- left meanwhile; onLeave owns the final write` is a real guard the first pass did not mention. It does not refute: it is a local-liveness check evaluated BEFORE the UpdateAsync rather than an ownership check inside the transform, and it exists on only one of the four trySave call sites (not on :238, :279, or :649).

The acquired token IS in memory and is simply never compared. tryLoad does `local data = migrate(stored)` then stamps `data._lock` at :118 and `captured = data`, so entry.data._lock holds this server's lock; `_lock` is absent from OWNED_FIELDS (:92-96) so it is never written back from `data`. The compare-and-swap is one line away and absent.

Two of the four write paths do not even check `dirty`: onLeave :277 `if not entry or entry.volatile or not store then return end` and BindToClose :645 `if not entry.volatile then` both write unconditionally. Only Profiles.flush :470 gates on `entry.dirty`. So a server holding an untouched stale copy still clobbers a newer owner.

Profiles.luau:103 `(now - (tonumber(lock.ts) or 0)) <= LOCK_STALE_SECONDS` — a lock whose `ts` is non-numeric or missing degrades to `now - 0`, far greater than 180, so a corrupted lock is instantly stealable rather than treated as held.

OVERSTATED SUPPORTING LEG: the finding labels EmoteService.luau:471 as [SOURCE] that 'both places write the same keys'. That line is a COMMENT, not code. `grep -rn "DataStoreService|UpdateAsync|GetAsync|SetAsync" dev-src` hits only dev-src/ServerScriptService/KenopsiaServer/Services/PartyRegistry.luau:56,90,114 (a party-code map); no profile store exists in any of dev-src's 22 .luau files, and dev-src/StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/KenopsiaClient/UI/Theme.luau:120 states '-- Session settings. No DataStore in the MVP by design'. Relabel as [SOURCE, comment only] / NEEDS_RUNTIME.

Studio cannot demonstrate this: game.JobId is "" in Studio, so :102 makes every lock look self-owned. NEEDS_RUNTIME — two live MainGame servers on the same userId, logging game.JobId and the incoming `stored._lock` inside both transforms, forcing server A's trySave to land after server B's tryLoad, then a GetAsync showing B's fields reverted and `_lock == nil`.

reviews.reasoning:
I tried to break this finding and could not. Every cited line number and every verbatim quote reproduces exactly against the live datamodel, and the two runtime claims I re-ran independently both replicated. PARTIAL stands. But I found one missed call site, one materially overstated causal claim, and one understatement, detailed below.

WHAT I RE-READ AND CONFIRMED

[SOURCE] I pulled live `game.ReplicatedFirst.KenopsiaLoading` lines 230-286 and 1-60 myself (lineCount 286, LocalScript). I hand-counted the returned block from its declared startLine=230 and every cited line lands exactly where the finding says: 242 `task.spawn(function()`, 245 `game.Loaded:Wait()`, 251 `local machineGui = playerGui:WaitForChild("KenopsiaMachine", 20)`, 252 `if machineGui then`, 253 `machineGui.Enabled = true`, 254 `local warning = machineGui:WaitForChild("Warning", 10)`, 268 `add(music and music:FindFirstChild("Intro"))`, 269 Loop, 270 SFX Warning, 271 Click, 272 `if #criticalAssets > 0 then`, 273-275 pcall wrapping 274 `ContentProvider:PreloadAsync(criticalAssets)`, 276 the warn, 283 `gui:Destroy()`, 284 `end)`. No off-by-one anywhere.

Structural claims verified, not taken on trust:
- No pcall around the coroutine body. The ONLY pcall in 242-284 is the inner one at 273-275 around PreloadAsync. `gui:Destroy()` at 283 is the last statement and the sole exit. Confirmed by reading, not by the prior pass's assertion.
- The cover really is opaque and full-screen: live 18-31 `gui.DisplayOrder = 100`, `gui.ResetOnSpawn = false`, `bg.Size = UDim2.fromScale(1, 1)`, `bg.BackgroundColor3 = INK` with no BackgroundTransparency assignment (default 0).
- No watchdog live. My own `search LoadingGui root=game` → 2 hits / 115 scripts (KenopsiaLoading:22 and the ServerStorage backup). Nothing else in the live place references it.

The two runtime claims replicated:
- [RUNTIME] `children game.SoundService.KenopsiaAudio.Music` → 2 children, `Loop` (Sound) and `Trials` (Folder). No `Intro`. Live:268 is a dead add. Confirmed.
- [RUNTIME] `children game.StarterGui.KenopsiaMachine` → 15 children (Status, Score, Selection, Info, RoundCard, Briefing, JoinCover, CountText, Announce, Fader, Scope, HipCross, SettingsPanel, HitMark, TouchControls). No `Warning`.

The audio hazard's precondition holds — I checked whether the `if #criticalAssets > 0` guard could save it. It cannot: [RUNTIME] `SFX` contains both `Click` and `Warning` as Sounds, and `Music.Loop` exists. criticalAssets is non-empty, so PreloadAsync definitely executes, upstream of teardown, inside a pcall that bounds errors but not yields. That half of the claim survives intact.

THE NEW FINDING IS NOT JUST CONFIRMED, IT IS UNDERSTATED. [RUNTIME] `search_name(query="Warning", root=game, maxResults=50)` → `count: 1`, the single result being `game.SoundService.KenopsiaAudio.SFX.Warning`, a Sound. There is no GUI object named Warning anywhere in the datamodel. [SOURCE] My own place-wide `search "Warning"` → 21 matches / 115 scripts, and not one is a creation — MachineLayout:34 and :410 are string-membership lists, :492 is a guarded FindFirstChild; RunnerClient:161 is a list; sorting:352/388 are sfx names. I read MachineLayout 405-432 directly: line 410 `local GROUPS = { "Warning", "SettingsPanel", ... }` sits under a comment saying "HunterLookSetup is built by KenopsiaClient at boot and adopted when it appears" — adoption of pre-existing frames, never construction. So the 10 s burn at live:254 is airtight.

WHAT THE PASS MISSED — CORRECTIONS

1. A SECOND CALL SITE EXISTS, in the repo but not live. [SOURCE] `studio-src/StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/MainMenu.client.luau:1525-1528`: `local deadline = os.clock() + 25` / `while playerGui:FindFirstChild("KenopsiaLoadingGui") and os.clock() < deadline do`. The pass's sweep for "KenopsiaLoading" was live-only and so declared "Nothing else in the place ever touches KenopsiaLoadingGui" — true as scoped to live, but incomplete. This does NOT refute "no watchdog": MainMenu only *waits* on the GUI and never destroys it, and its wait is deadline-bounded. And [RUNTIME] `children game.StarterPlayer.StarterPlayerScripts` → 15 children, MainMenu is NOT among them, yet [SOURCE] `default.project.json:111` maps it. So MainMenu is repo-only, un-deployed.

2. THE "BRICKED CLIENT" IS LATENT, NOT REACHABLE — the finding overstates it. It offers live:253 `machineGui.Enabled = true` as the example thrower. That line cannot throw: [RUNTIME] `get game.StarterGui.KenopsiaMachine` → `className: "ScreenGui"`, `Enabled: false`. It is a real ScreenGui (shipped disabled, so 253 is load-bearing), and assigning `.Enabled` on it is valid. I walked every statement in 242-283 and none can realistically raise with the current place contents: os.clock, game:IsLoaded, Loaded:Wait, two timeout-form WaitForChilds (which return nil, never throw), guarded property writes, table ops, FindFirstChild, a pcall'd PreloadAsync, task.wait, Destroy. The missing-pcall/single-exit structure is genuinely there and is a real defense-in-depth gap, but it should be reported as latent fragility, not as a live black-screen defect. This is the one place the finding's framing outruns its evidence.

3. THE 10 s STALL HAPPENS TWICE, from a second script. [SOURCE] live `game.StarterPlayer.StarterPlayerScripts.KenopsiaClient:3751` `local warningFrame = machine:WaitForChild("Warning", 10)` — same nonexistent object, same 10 s timeout, different script. Off the loading-teardown path, but same root cause, so the missing `Warning` object costs more than the pass accounted for.

4. AN UNCITED FLOOR. Neither pass mentions live:281 `if held < 2 then task.wait(2 - held) end`, a deliberate 2 s minimum hold immediately before `done = true` / `gui:Destroy()`. It bounds nothing (it is a floor, not a ceiling) but it belongs in any load-time accounting: total ≈ max(2 s, game.Loaded + 10 s Warning stall + preload), i.e. the Warning stall dominates. This strengthens the new finding.

5. THE FORWARD-LOOKING HAZARD IS CONDITIONAL, NOT CERTAIN. I verified the mirror block ([SOURCE] `studio-src/ReplicatedFirst/KenopsiaLoading.client.luau:137-143`, `local menuGui = playerGui:FindFirstChild("KenopsiaMenu")` … `for _, d in ipairs(menuRoot:GetDescendants())`) and `default.project.json:9` — both quoted correctly. So after a sync, whether menuRoot is non-nil when KenopsiaLoading reads it is a race between ReplicatedFirst and StarterPlayerScripts — likely won by KenopsiaLoading's own 10 s stall, but not guaranteed. "Would enlarge the preload set" should read "would likely enlarge".

reviews.reasoning:
Both consequences the claim predicts fail against the live code, and the one real defect is the opposite in kind of what the claim asserts.

SCENARIO A (bricked black screen) CANNOT OCCUR. I read live 230-286 verbatim off weppy clientId ad22f53b / placeId 110672791536316 and enumerated every statement between `task.spawn(function()` (live:242) and `gui:Destroy()` (live:283). There is not one throwable expression outside the pcall. Both WaitForChild calls carry timeouts (20, 10), so they RETURN NIL on expiry rather than raising. `machineGui` is nil-guarded at live:252. Every instance access afterwards is either nil-guarded or a short-circuit `x and x:FindFirstChild(...)`. `warn` cannot raise. The only raising call, PreloadAsync, is inside the pcall.

Decisively: the finding nominates live:253 `machineGui.Enabled = true` as its example error site. [RUNTIME] `query_instances get game.StarterGui.KenopsiaMachine` returns `"className": "ScreenGui"`. `Enabled` is a valid ScreenGui property and the variable is non-nil by the guard on 252, so that line is provably incapable of throwing. The finding's flagship mechanism has no trigger, therefore the permanent-black-screen consequence is not producible.

SCENARIO B (indefinite audio hold) IS UNESTABLISHED. The batch is at most 4 items: GrungeWash ([RUNTIME] find_child → found, ImageLabel), Music.Loop, SFX.Warning, SFX.Click. [RUNTIME] `children game.SoundService.KenopsiaAudio.Music` → childCount 2 (Loop, Trials): the finding is right that the `Intro` add is dead. But "indefinitely" is an assertion about ContentProvider's internal request/timeout behavior, which is not readable from source — the finding concedes this itself ("not provable from source"). An unbounded-by-this-code yield is not the same as a demonstrated player-facing hang, and the review supplied no runtime observation of one.

THE FORWARD-LOOKING HAZARD IS REFUTED OUTRIGHT. Mirror studio-src/ReplicatedFirst/KenopsiaLoading.client.luau:137-139 gates the extra block on `local menuGui = playerGui:FindFirstChild("KenopsiaMenu")` / `local menuRoot = menuGui and menuGui:FindFirstChild("Root")` / `if menuRoot then`. [RUNTIME] `search_name("KenopsiaMenu", root=game)` on placeId 110672791536316 returns `"count": 0`. StarterGui holds exactly three ScreenGuis (KenopsiaMachine, FieldPushGui, KenopsiaEmote), and an independent grep of the live 3760-line KenopsiaClient dump finds zero KenopsiaMenu references. So a Rojo sync into MainGame leaves menuRoot nil and the loop never executes — it adds ZERO assets.
